   - Use multiple agents when: the scope is uncertain, multiple areas of the codebase are involved, or you need to understand existing patterns before planning.
   - Quality over quantity - 3 agents maximum, but you should try to use the minimum number of agents necessary (usually just 1)
   - If using multiple agents: Provide each agent with a specific search focus or area to explore. Example: One agent searches for existing implementations, another explores related components, a third investigating testing patterns

Launch Plan agent(s) to design the implementation based on the user's intent and your exploration results from Phase 1.

You can launch up to 1 agent(s) in parallel.

- Include only your recommended approach, not all alternatives
- Ensure that the plan file is concise enough to scan quickly, but detailed enough to execute effectively
- Name the critical files to be modified. For changes that repeat a pattern across many files, describe the pattern once and list a few representative paths — do not enumerate every file or line number
- Reference existing functions and utilities you found that should be reused, with their file paths
- Include a verification section describing how to test the changes end-to-end (run the code, use MCP tools, run tests)

### Phase 5: Call ExitPlanMode
At the very end of your turn, once you have asked the user questions and are happy with your final plan file - you should always call ExitPlanMode to indicate to the user that you are done planning.
This is critical - your turn should only end with either using the AskUserQuestion tool OR calling ExitPlanMode. Do not stop unless it's for these 2 reasons

**Important:** Use AskUserQuestion ONLY to clarify requirements or choose between approaches. Use ExitPlanMode to request plan approval. Do NOT ask about plan approval in any other way - no text questions, no AskUserQuestion. Phrases like "Is this plan okay?", "Should I proceed?", "How does this plan look?", "Any changes before we start?", or similar MUST use ExitPlanMode.

NOTE: At any point in time through this workflow you should feel free to ask the user questions or clarifications using the AskUserQuestion tool. Don't make large assumptions about user intent. The goal is to present a well researched plan to the user, and tie any loose ends before implementation begins.

input.prompt:
Repo: /home/crash/docs/school/cs370/CS370-Term-Project ("carwatch", Raspberry Pi in-car OBD2 diagnostic recorder, CS370 OS project). Thoroughness: very thorough. READ-ONLY.

Context: the current documented plan (decision D-015, docs/DECISIONS.md §A.1) is a USB OBD2 adapter (ELM327/STN chip) plugged into the Pi, appearing as /dev/obd via a udev rule. Earlier plans (now superseded) used raw CAN via an MCP2515 on SPI. The team now wants to pivot to: a Bluetooth Classic OBD2 adapter (ELM327-style, Serial Port Profile / RFCOMM, explicitly NOT BLE) plugged into the car's OBD2 port, with the Pi (powered from the car's USB) reading it over Bluetooth serial (e.g. /dev/rfcomm0). The pivot should simplify things.

Find EVERY place the hardware/data path is described or assumed, across all tracked files (git ls-files), including: docs/*.md, docs/DECISIONS.md, docs/hardware/* (BOM.md, wiring.md, pid-survey.md, schematic-conventions.md, etc.), docs/BOARD/board.toml item bodies, README.md, CLAUDE.md, Makefile, scripts/, src/ (esp. src/obd/), include/, tests/, tools/, electricalDrawing/ (just list files and what blocks they describe; KiCad files are text), soak/.

Search terms at least: USB adapter, ELM327, STN, OBDLink, /dev/obd, udev, tty, serial, MCP2515, SPI, CAN, TJA1050, Bluetooth, BLE, rfcomm, SPP, pair, USB-C, power, 12 V, obdsim, pty, GPIO, LED, schematic.

Report, grouped by file:
- file:line ranges and a one-line summary of what each passage claims about the hardware path
- classify each as: (A) already compatible with a Bluetooth-serial adapter, (B) needs rewording (USB adapter -> Bluetooth SPP adapter, /dev/obd -> rfcomm), (C) about the superseded MCP2515/CAN path (should stay only in the superseded/stretch history), (D) code or build logic that would change.
Also report: what src/obd/ currently contains (files, whether it opens a tty, termios settings), what scripts/ contains, what the KiCad schematic's blocks are (power, CAN, Pi interface, LED?), and the BOM items/prices. And any board.toml items (slug + title) about the adapter, udev, CAN, hardware ordering (`order`), PID survey (`pidhonda`, `oilq`), power.
Keep the report under ~1500 words, precise file:line references.

Both maps are in, and two findings shape the plan:
- The only real logic that changes is in `scripts/provision_pi.sh`. `src/obd/main.c` is still a stub.

Two questions before I write it up:

questions.question: Which Bluetooth Classic (SPP) adapter is the plan built on? The board shows the USB adapter's bring-up (`bench`) and first capture (`firstcap`) as done.

options.label: Buy OBDLink LX (Recommended)
options.description: An STN-chip Bluetooth Classic adapter; the same chip family D-015 preferred, and more reliable than clones. The USB adapter stays documented as the fallback, since both speak the same ELM327 protocol.

options.label: Already own a BT ELM327
options.description: A generic Bluetooth ELM327 is on hand. The BOM records it; the clone-reliability risk is written into the decision.

options.label: Own one, model TBD
options.description: I'll record a placeholder and a board item to note the model and PIN once it is in hand.

questions.question: Once CLAUDE.md is condensed, where should the moved rationale (why commits are sized this way, the merge-gate question set, repo settings, grading consequences) live?

options.label: One new docs/PROCESS.md (Recommended)

# Plan: Bluetooth OBD2 pivot + condensed CLAUDE.md reference chain

## Context

Two problems:

- **CLAUDE.md is too big.** It is 567 lines (about 28 KB, about 7k tokens) and loads every
  session.
  - It restates facts that live in authoritative docs elsewhere: the session checklist
    appears three times, the board workflow four times, the ownership map three times and
    the transcript copy-out five times.
  - Several copies disagree:
    - board paths still say `docs/board.toml` in about 20 places;
    - the transcript cadence is given as "every milestone" in one place and "every
      session" in another;
    - the banned commit-message list differs between two files;
    - the three ownership maps differ;
    - the §7.4 example cites mechanism F, which is no longer committed.
- **The hardware plan is changing.**
  - **New plan (Camden, 2026-09-23):** a **Bluetooth Classic (SPP/RFCOMM, not BLE) OBD2
    adapter, OBDLink LX (STN chip)**, plugged into the car. The Pi is powered from the
    car's USB and uses its **built-in Bluetooth** to read the adapter.
  - **What it changes:** it simplifies the box to one power cable. It supersedes D-015
    (the USB adapter), which stays documented as the fallback because it speaks the same
    ELM327 protocol.
  - **Little to change in code:** `src/obd/main.c` is a stub, and only the TODO scaffold
    in `scripts/provision_pi.sh` has transport logic.

**Goal:** CLAUDE.md becomes a short, rules-only index. Each fact has **one** home that
people and Claude both follow, and every live doc describes the Bluetooth plan without
discarding the reasoning history.

## Shape: 3 steps, 2 new PRs (+ 2 earlier ones pushed)

### Step 0: Unblock main (prerequisite)

- **Board fix.** Branch `camden/m1/boardmerge` from main and restore the two lines that
  the `8e8c74a` merge dropped from `docs/BOARD/board.toml` (~line 530): `'''` and
  `[[item]]`. Verify with `python tools/test_board.py` and
  `python tools/board_sync.py --status`.
- **Board items.** Add `[[item]]`s so every PR traces to an issue: `boardmerge`,
  `memopolish`, `mdlint` (decision D-018), `btpivot` (D-019) and `claudeindex`.
  - **What sync writes:** `python tools/board_sync.py` creates the GitHub issues.
- **Open PRs.** Push `boardmerge`, `problem-polish` and `mdlint`, and open them as drafts.
  - **Bodies:** each from the PR template, with `Closes #n`.
  - **Missing output:** the pasted `make` sections will say that make and gcc are not
    installed on this machine. They must be run on the Pi or on Lance's machine before
    the PR is marked ready.
- **Stacking.** `problem-polish` and `mdlint` are based on main. Both say they need the
  board fix to go green.

### PR A: `camden/m1/bt-adapter`: "M1 docs: read OBD2 over a Bluetooth Classic adapter"

Based on `mdlint`, which it depends on for D-018 and the lint config; the PR says so.
Closes `btpivot`.

1. **Decision commit** (`docs/DECISIONS.md` only, one responsibility: the decision
   record).
   - **New decision.** Add **§A.1 D-019**: "The Pi reads OBD2 through a Bluetooth Classic
     (SPP) adapter; the USB adapter is the fallback."
     - **Attribution:** By: Camden (in session) + Claude. ⚠️ UNREVIEWED, with a review
       queue row for Lance.
     - **Cites G.1 (D-001):** G.1 rejected a Bluetooth ELM327 because it gives up
       interrupts and bus timing. D-015 already accepted exactly that cost, so Bluetooth
       loses nothing further.
     - **Gains:** one cable; no USB data cable crossing the cabin; the same Mode 01
       protocol.
     - **Costs:** pairing and bind provisioning; link-drop failure modes; and the Pi 4's
       single Wi-Fi/Bluetooth chip also runs D-013's access point, a coexistence risk
       that needs measuring.
     - **Stable device name:** keep `/dev/obd` via
       `rfcomm bind 0 <MAC> 1` + a udev symlink `rfcomm0 → obd`. Nothing downstream
       changes, and falling back to USB is a one-rule swap.
   - **Supersede D-015.** Move old §A.1 (D-015) to **§G.4, 🗑 superseded by D-019**,
     with its text kept.
   - **Reword live entries** that say "USB adapter" or "USB cable":
     - A.6: "one box, one cable";
     - A.7;
     - B.1: interrupts now belong to the kernel's Bluetooth/RFCOMM stack; same argument;
     - B.4: the phone still never pairs, but the Pi now pairs with the adapter.
2. **Live-doc commit** (the enactment: one question applied consistently, §7.3 doc
   rule). Reword every class-B passage from the hardware sweep:
   - `README.md`
   - `docs/DESIGN.md`:
     - diagram box and arrow;
     - failure row at line 74: the link drops, RFCOMM returns `EIO`/`POLLHUP`, and the
       reader reconnects with backoff instead of waiting on udev;
     - line 111.
   - `docs/hardware/wiring.md`: adapter table and bring-up steps (`bluetoothctl`
     pair/trust, `rfcomm bind`, then `ATZ`).
   - `docs/hardware/BOM.md`: OBDLink LX (price marked "verify"); the USB unit listed as
     fallback.
   - `docs/hardware/pid-survey.md`: `screen /dev/obd`, no baud.
   - `docs/hardware/schematic-conventions.md`:
     - the CAN block and SPI0/interrupt pins move to a "stretch only" note;
     - live blocks are Power + LED.
   - `docs/PLAN.md`
   - `docs/milestones.md`: the M1 stretch criterion.
3. **Scaffold commit** (code comments/TODOs only, Camden's area):
   - `src/obd/main.c` header and TODO: RFCOMM tty, hangup detection;
   - `scripts/provision_pi.sh` TODO: `bluez`, pair/trust, a persistent `rfcomm bind`
     unit, and a udev symlink replacing the USB vendor/product rule;
   - `tools/pidscan.py` docstring.
4. **Board commit** (`docs/BOARD/board.toml`):
   - **Rewrite the bodies of open items** that assume USB: `pidhonda`, `oilq`, `canreq`,
     `obdsim`, `pisensor`, `keyoff`.
   - **Add items:**
     - `btorder`: buy the OBDLink LX (hardware, owner Camden);
     - `btbench`: pair and bind on the Pi with no car, `ATZ` answers on `/dev/obd`
       (task, blocked by `btorder`);
     - `btcoex`: measure access-point + RFCOMM coexistence (hardware).
   - **Leave done items unedited** (`bench`, `order`, `firstcap`): they are history.
   - Add `rfcomm` and `bluetoothctl` to `cspell.json` in the same commit that first uses
     them.

### PR B: `camden/m1/claude-index`: "M1 docs: condense CLAUDE.md into a rules-only index"

Based on PR A, so it describes the Bluetooth plan. Closes `claudeindex`. Target is about
170 lines and about 8 KB, roughly a 70% cut.

**Keep the section numbers §0–§11 and §7.1–§7.12 as stable anchors.** About 40 existing
references depend on them, in DECISIONS, board.toml, the PR template, `.gitmessage` and
commit history. Each section shrinks to its binding rules plus a **→ pointer** to the one
doc that holds the detail.

| CLAUDE.md § | Keeps (rules Claude follows every session) | Detail moves to (single home) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Header | 3 lines + the **reference chain**: CLAUDE.md → `docs/README.md` (topic index) → source doc | — |
| §0 | **The** start *and* end checklist (merges §0, §7.7 and §7.11's session end; adds the transcript copy-out every session) | removed from §7.7/§7.11 and PLAN.md §4 |
| §1 | command list + the DONE rule | `docs/BOARD/BOARD.md` for sync flags |
| §2 | the 8 hard constraints, verbatim (graded) | — |
| §3–§5 | 4 lines: product, testbed, claim, mechanisms D+E, pipeline | README, DECISIONS A.1/A.2/B.1/§D |
| §6 | one ownership table, including `electricalDrawing/` | DESIGN §7 mirrors it (graded M2 deliverable) |
| §7.1 | the five absolutes, verbatim | — |
| §7.2–§7.5 | branch naming; the one-sentence commit test; tests in the same commit; no content+reflow mix; every commit builds; message format → `.gitmessage`; PR → template, draft early, `[cross]`, pasted output | `docs/PROCESS.md` (why, examples, size smells) |
| §7.6 | "reviewer must understand every line" + where the question set lives | PROCESS.md, PR template checklist |
| §7.7 | "Claude never marks a decision reviewed/LOCKED" | checklist moved to §0 |
| §7.8 | stop triggers → add a board item | BOARD.md |
| §7.9–§7.10 | one line each | PROCESS.md (volume, repo settings) |
| §7.11 | never touch issues by hand; blockers become `[[item]]`; only Ready; sync at session end | BOARD.md (labels, columns, deps, CI; the label table moves there if missing) |
| §7.12 | SVG + `hwcheck` output in PR; never hand-write `.kicad_pcb` | `docs/hardware/schematic-conventions.md` |
| §8 | the 8 workflow rules, one line each (evidence-over-assertion kept whole) | prompt example → PROCESS.md |
| §9–§11 | one line each | transcripts/README, PROMPTLOG, milestones M5, board |

**Commits in PR B:**

1. **Stale paths.** Replace `docs/board.toml`, `docs/BOARD.md` and
   `docs/board.lock.json` with `docs/BOARD/…` everywhere:
   - docs: README, milestones, PLAN, DECISIONS, tools/README, BOARD.md;
   - code: `board.yml`, the Makefile comment, the `test_board.py` docstring and the
     `board_sync.py` footer string.
   - **Why it goes first:** it is mechanical, reviewed separately, and later diffs stay
     clean.
2. **Create `docs/PROCESS.md`.** Move the rationale out of CLAUDE §7 verbatim, with no
   rewording, so the move is reviewable:
   - the §7.3 prose;
   - the §7.4 example, with its stale mechanism-F citation replaced by a mechanism-D
     one;
   - the §7.6 question set and the §7.9–§7.10 text;
   - the §7.11 defense rationale;
   - the §8 prompt example.
3. **Condense CLAUDE.md** to the table above. Then:
   - point DECISIONS F.1's summary at CLAUDE.md §7 + PROCESS.md, adding one sentence and
     leaving the locked content unchanged;
   - remove PLAN.md §4's duplicate ritual in favor of a pointer.
4. **Rebuild `docs/README.md`** as the single topic index for people and Claude. For each
   topic, it names the **source** doc:
   - it adds the missing entries: tools/README, soak/README, `.gitmessage`, the PR
     template, the lint configs and the transcripts READMEs;
   - it resolves the ownership ambiguity.
5. **Align small contradictions:**
   - `.gitmessage` banned list and area list: add `process`, which history already uses;
   - transcript cadence: every session;
   - the milestones.md "VERIFY THESE DATES" banner, dropped because M0 checked it off.

**Out of scope, but filed as board items:**

- tracked `.kicad_prl` and `.history` (Lance's area);
- DECISIONS F.2 (🔒 LOCKED) omits `electricalDrawing/`. Reopening it needs a human yes,
  so it gets a `decision` item instead of an edit.

## Rules honored

- Every decision made in session goes in as ⚠️ UNREVIEWED in the commit that implements
  it.
- No LOCKED text is rewritten.
- Explicit `git add` paths only.
- Every file is read in full before it is committed.
- Every commit keeps markdownlint and cSpell at zero, using the D-018 configs and the
  saved lint memory.

## Verification (per commit and per PR)

- **Lint:** markdownlint 0.41.1 with `.markdownlint.jsonc` over every tracked `.md`,
  0 findings; cspell over every tracked file, 0 findings. Both run via
  `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 /usr/share/code/code` from the scratchpad installs.
- **Board:** `python tools/test_board.py` passes, and
  `python tools/board_sync.py --check --no-board` shows no drift in the milestone table.
- **Code:** `python -m py_compile tools/*.py`; `bash -n scripts/provision_pi.sh`.
- **Link check:** a script resolves every relative markdown link and every
  `CLAUDE.md §x.y` citation in the repo against the new headings, with 0 dangling.
- **Size:** `wc -c CLAUDE.md` before and after, reported in PR B.
- **Content preservation:** each paragraph removed from CLAUDE.md is traced to its new
  home, as a table in the PR B body.
- **Stated gap:** `make`, `make test` and `make asan` cannot run on this machine (no
  make or gcc). Each PR stays a draft until a partner pastes that output.

1	# docs/board.toml — the single source of truth for the carwatch GitHub board.
2	#
3	# CONTRACT
4	#   This file describes what SHOULD exist on GitHub. `tools/board_sync.py` makes
5	#   GitHub match it. The sync is a reconciler, not a generator:
6	#
7	#     * running it twice changes nothing the second time
8	#     * items absent from this file are left completely alone (never closed,
9	#       never edited, never removed from the board) — they are reported as
10	#       unmanaged and ignored
11	#     * adding one task means adding one [[item]] block and re-running sync
12	#     * `slug` is the permanent identity of an item. Issue numbers live in
13	#       docs/board.lock.json and are derived, never typed here.
14	#
15	#   Inside an issue body the sync owns ONLY the region between the
16	#   <!-- board-sync:deps --> markers. Everything else in a body on GitHub is
17	#   overwritten from this file, so edit prose HERE, not in the web UI.
18	#
19	# EDITING
20	#   status = backlog | blocked | ready | in-progress | in-review | done
21	#     Omit it and sync picks the column for you: "backlog" while any blocker is
22	#     still open, "ready" once nothing blocks it, "done" once the issue closes.
23	#     Set it explicitly to drive the column by hand — "blocked" is reserved for
24	#     waiting on something that is not another item (a shipment, a reply).
25	#   done      closes the issue. Items labeled question/decision additionally
26	#             require --close-questions, because CLAUDE.md forbids Claude from
27	#             closing those on its own judgement.
28	#   blocked_by takes slugs, never issue numbers.
29	#   decision  optional "D-###". Must exist in docs/DECISIONS.md; sync renders a
30	#             link line into the managed region and warns about unknown IDs.
31	#
32	# Run:  python tools/board_sync.py --check     (report drift, change nothing)
33	#       python tools/board_sync.py             (reconcile)
34	
35	[board]

233	Handout §5: 'The 48-hour soak and the live demonstration run on live sensors.'
234	A soak on our fake OBD2 port (`obdsim`) is synthesized data by that definition.

241	
242	> Subject: CS370 term project — 48-hour soak against a simulated OBD2 port
243	>
244	> Professor Pallickara,
245	>
246	> Camden Thomas and Lance Baron. Our term project is an in-vehicle diagnostic
247	> recorder: a Pi reading a 2015 Honda CR-V's own sensors through a USB OBD2
248	> adapter and learning that car's normal, so it can flag developing faults that a
249	> fixed maintenance interval misses.
250	>
251	> A car cannot run for 48 continuous hours, so we are building a simulated OBD2
252	> port that answers the same requests the car does, from recorded drives. §5 says
253	> the soak runs on live sensors, and we read a simulated port as synthesized data.
254	> Every record it produces is labeled synth. Three ways we could go:
255	>
256	> 1. Soak against the simulated port, labeled synth throughout the logs, report

264	> prefer option 3 we would like to know now, while the design is cheap to change.

267	> Camden Thomas & Lance Baron

# docs/board.toml — the single source of truth for the carwatch GitHub board.
#
# CONTRACT
#   This file describes what SHOULD exist on GitHub. `tools/board_sync.py` makes
#   GitHub match it. The sync is a reconciler, not a generator:
#
#     * running it twice changes nothing the second time
#     * items absent from this file are left completely alone (never closed,
#       never edited, never removed from the board) — they are reported as
#       unmanaged and ignored
#     * adding one task means adding one [[item]] block and re-running sync
#     * `slug` is the permanent identity of an item. Issue numbers live in
#       docs/board.lock.json and are derived, never typed here.
#
#   Inside an issue body the sync owns ONLY the region between the
#   <!-- board-sync:deps --> markers. Everything else in a body on GitHub is
#   overwritten from this file, so edit prose HERE, not in the web UI.
#
# EDITING
#   status = backlog | blocked | ready | in-progress | in-review | done
#     Omit it and sync picks the column for you: "backlog" while any blocker is
#     still open, "ready" once nothing blocks it, "done" once the issue closes.
#     Set it explicitly to drive the column by hand — "blocked" is reserved for
#     waiting on something that is not another item (a shipment, a reply).
#   done      closes the issue. Items labeled question/decision additionally
#             require --close-questions, because CLAUDE.md forbids Claude from
#             closing those on its own judgement.
#   blocked_by takes slugs, never issue numbers.
#   decision  optional "D-###". Must exist in docs/DECISIONS.md; sync renders a
#             link line into the managed region and warns about unknown IDs.
#
# Run:  python tools/board_sync.py --check     (report drift, change nothing)
#       python tools/board_sync.py             (reconcile)

[board]
# Identified by NUMBER, not title: matching on a name is how you end up writing to
# one project while reading another in the browser. This is the project linked to
# the repository — the one the repo's Projects tab opens.
number = 1
title = "carwatch"
columns = ["Backlog", "Ready", "In progress", "In review", "Done"]
# Sync maps board.toml statuses onto whatever Status options the project has
# (COLUMN_PREFERENCE in board_sync.py) rather than rewriting the field, because
# rewriting it discards every card's current value. `blocked` therefore lands in
# Backlog here, which is what we want anyway. Set reshape_status = true only to
# deliberately rebuild the Status field from `columns`.
# reshape_status = false

[people]
camden = "CamdenThomas"
lance = "Lance-Baron"

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ labels

[[label]]
name = "question"
color = "d876e3"
description = "Needs a human answer. Claude may never close this."

[[label]]
name = "decision"
color = "8250df"
description = "A design choice that must be made. Claude may never close this."

[[label]]
name = "task"
color = "0e8a16"
description = "Work to be done."

[[label]]
name = "bug"
color = "d73a4a"
description = "Something is wrong."

[[label]]
name = "hardware"
color = "e99695"
description = "Physical world: order it, wire it, measure it, drive it."

[[label]]
name = "blocked"
color = "000000"
description = "Waiting on a dependency. Applied and removed by board_sync."

[[label]]
name = "critical-path"
color = "b60205"
description = "Slipping this slips the project."

# -------------------------------------------------------------- milestones
# Dates assume an Aug 24 2026 semester start — see PLAN.md / decision D-008.
# Issue `dates` exists to verify this.
#
# THIS IS THE ONLY PLACE MILESTONE DATES ARE WRITTEN. The table in
# docs/milestones.md is regenerated from these blocks between its
# <!-- board-sync:milestones --> markers, and the GitHub milestone due dates are
# patched in place. Correct a date here, re-run sync, and all three agree.
# `deliverable` is used for both the GitHub milestone description and the table.

[[milestone]]
name = "M0"
due = "2026-09-20"
week = "4"
hours = "2–3"
deliverable = "Team formed; hardware ordered; repo + CLAUDE.md initialized"

[[milestone]]
name = "M1"
due = "2026-09-27"
week = "5"
hours = "3–4"
deliverable = "Problem memo; each partner's `.jsonl` transcripts copied out"

[[milestone]]
name = "M2"
due = "2026-10-11"
week = "6–7"
hours = "8–10"
deliverable = "Design document; both sensors electrically alive; **baseline collection starts**"

[[milestone]]
name = "M3"
due = "2026-11-01"
week = "8–10"
hours = "25–30"
deliverable = "Checkpoint demo: both sensors through the real pipeline into real storage; ≥1 menu mechanism working"

[[milestone]]
name = "M4"
due = "2026-11-29"
week = "11–14"
hours = "30–40"
deliverable = "Feature freeze; 48-hour soak begins"

[[milestone]]
name = "M5"
due = "2026-12-06"
week = "15"
hours = "10–14"
deliverable = "Final submission: system, soak logs, evaluation report, process artifacts, complete transcripts"

[[milestone]]
name = "M6"
due = "2026-12-18"
week = "15–16"
hours = "—"
deliverable = "Demo day: live demo, fault injection, individual defenses (date assumed — see `dates`)"

# =============================================================== M0 items

milestone = "M0"
labels = ["task"]

status = "done"
title = "M0 admin: register the team as Camden Thomas + Lance Baron"

'''

labels = ["hardware", "critical-path"]
owner = "camden"
title = "M0 hardware: order the core BOM, USB OBD2 adapter first"
body = '''
See docs/hardware/BOM.md — Pi 4, 32GB A2 microSD x2, a USB OBD2 adapter with an STN
chip (e.g. OBDLink SX, D-015), a 12V-socket USB-C adapter (>= 5.1V / 3A) + cable, the
LED and resistor. ~$125.

**The OBD2 adapter is the whole data path.** The PID survey, the bench bring-up and
every capture after them run on it, and the PID survey answers the project's named
risk.

Critical path B. The handout names shipping time as the most common silent
schedule-killer, twice. Blocks every piece of physical work in the project.

Done when: order confirmations are in the thread and ETAs are noted here.
'''

[[item]]
slug = "honda"
milestone = "M0"
labels = ["question", "critical-path"]
owner = "lance"
decision = "D-007"
title = "M0 question: confirm the Honda's year, model, engine and transmission"
body = '''
Blocks the PID survey (and therefore diagnostic #1).

Need: year, model, engine, transmission.

**Answered 2026-09-21 (Camden, in session): 2015 Honda CR-V EX-L.** By model year:
2.4 L direct-injected K24W with a CVT; FWD/AWD not recorded. Lance: confirm the engine
and drivetrain from the VIN or door-jamb sticker, sign D-007 in docs/DECISIONS.md §A.3,
then close this issue.
'''

[[item]]
slug = "dates"
milestone = "M0"
labels = ["question"]
owner = "camden"
decision = "D-008"
title = "M0 question: verify M0-M6 dates against the syllabus"
body = '''
docs/milestones.md assumes an Aug 24 2026 semester start, which puts M0 due
2026-09-20. The handout gives week numbers, not dates.

If the assumption is off by even one week, the M4 soak start moves — and M4
already lands on Thanksgiving week.

Answer: paste the real milestone dates. Then correct docs/milestones.md and the
[[milestone]] due dates in docs/board.toml, and re-run board_sync. Decision D-008.

**Answered 2026-09-21 (Camden, milestones.md check-off):** the dates in board.toml
are correct as written. Camden: mark D-008 LOCKED in your own commit, then close this
issue (question label — needs `--close-questions`).
'''

[[item]]
slug = "soakq"
milestone = "M0"
labels = ["decision", "critical-path"]
owner = "camden"
decision = "D-006"
title = "M0 decision: 48-hour soak on a fake OBD2 port — ask Pallickara"
body = '''
Handout §5: 'The 48-hour soak and the live demonstration run on live sensors.'
A soak on our fake OBD2 port (`obdsim`) is synthesized data by that definition.
Options (a) exception, (b) live Pi-side sensor + synth OBD, (c) parked car on the
live port — DECISIONS.md §E.3.

**Build as if the answer is no.** Fallback is (b), which `pisensor` decides.

**Email — edit into your own voice, send from Camden with Lance cc'd:**

> Subject: CS370 term project — 48-hour soak against a simulated OBD2 port
>
> Professor Pallickara,
>
> Camden Thomas and Lance Baron. Our term project is an in-vehicle diagnostic
> recorder: a Pi reading a 2015 Honda CR-V's own sensors through a USB OBD2
> adapter and learning that car's normal, so it can flag developing faults that a
> fixed maintenance interval misses.
>
> A car cannot run for 48 continuous hours, so we are building a simulated OBD2
> port that answers the same requests the car does, from recorded drives. §5 says
> the soak runs on live sensors, and we read a simulated port as synthesized data.
> Every record it produces is labeled synth. Three ways we could go:
>
> 1. Soak against the simulated port, labeled synth throughout the logs, report
>    and demo.
> 2. Add a sensor to the Pi itself (an accelerometer and a temperature probe) that
>    runs live for all 48 hours while the OBD side is simulated and labeled.
> 3. Soak in the parked car on the live port with a battery tender.
>
> We are building toward option 2 by default. If option 1 is acceptable it saves
> hardware time we would rather spend on the analysis and the evaluation; if you
> prefer option 3 we would like to know now, while the design is cheap to change.
>
> Thank you,
> Camden Thomas & Lance Baron

Decision D-006. Must close before M4.
'''

[[item]]
slug = "ghsetup"
milestone = "M0"

[[item]]
slug = "boardpath"
milestone = "M1"
labels = ["bug", "critical-path"]
owner = "camden"
title = "M1 tools: board_sync still looks for docs/board.toml after the move to docs/BOARD/"
body = '''
`make test` and `make asan` are RED on main, and have been since the board files
moved. Every gate in CLAUDE.md 1 runs through this target, so nothing can be
declared DONE until it is fixed.

    $ make test
    boundary                     PASS
    board.toml                   FAIL
      manifest not found: .../CS370-Term-Project/docs/board.toml
    make: *** [Makefile:67: boardcheck] Error 1

WHAT BROKE IT
Commit e42b28d ("m1 touch up") moved the three board files into a subdirectory:

    docs/board.toml       -> docs/BOARD/board.toml
    docs/board.lock.json  -> docs/BOARD/board.lock.json
    docs/BOARD.md         -> docs/BOARD/BOARD.md

`tools/board_sync.py` still resolves the manifest as `<repo>/docs/board.toml`,
so board_sync.py, test_board.py (through it), the boardcheck target and the
board.yml CI workflow all fail. `python tools/board_sync.py --status` is dead
too, which is the command CLAUDE.md 0 tells every session to start with.

OPTIONS
  1. Point the path constants in board_sync.py at docs/BOARD/. One-line fix,
     keeps e42b28d's tidier layout.
  2. Revert the move; put the three files back at docs/. Also one line, but
     undoes a human's deliberate reorganisation.
  RECOMMEND 1 — the move was intentional and the code is what is stale.

WHAT UNBLOCKS IT
Nothing: this is a task, not a question. It is filed rather than fixed inline
because CLAUDE.md 7.2 forbids folding unrelated work into an open branch, and
it was found while doing the M1 transcript copy-out (tx1 / #17).

ALSO NOTE, same root cause
`tools/test_board.py` needs Python 3.11+ for `tomllib`. The department machines
default to `python3` = 3.9.25, so the target dies with ModuleNotFoundError
before it ever reports the path problem. Either set `PY ?= python3.11` in the
Makefile or fall back to `tomli`. Worth folding into the same fix.
'''

1	# docs/board.toml — the single source of truth for the carwatch GitHub board.
2	#
3	# CONTRACT
4	#   This file describes what SHOULD exist on GitHub. `tools/board_sync.py` makes
5	#   GitHub match it. The sync is a reconciler, not a generator:
6	#
7	#     * running it twice changes nothing the second time
8	#     * items absent from this file are left completely alone (never closed,
9	#       never edited, never removed from the board) — they are reported as
10	#       unmanaged and ignored
11	#     * adding one task means adding one [[item]] block and re-running sync
12	#     * `slug` is the permanent identity of an item. Issue numbers live in
13	#       docs/board.lock.json and are derived, never typed here.
14	#
15	#   Inside an issue body the sync owns ONLY the region between the
16	#   <!-- board-sync:deps --> markers. Everything else in a body on GitHub is
17	#   overwritten from this file, so edit prose HERE, not in the web UI.
18	#
19	# EDITING
20	#   status = backlog | blocked | ready | in-progress | in-review | done
21	#     Omit it and sync picks the column for you: "backlog" while any blocker is
22	#     still open, "ready" once nothing blocks it, "done" once the issue closes.
23	#     Set it explicitly to drive the column by hand — "blocked" is reserved for
24	#     waiting on something that is not another item (a shipment, a reply).
25	#   done      closes the issue. Items labeled question/decision additionally
26	#             require --close-questions, because CLAUDE.md forbids Claude from
27	#             closing those on its own judgement.
28	#   blocked_by takes slugs, never issue numbers.
29	#   decision  optional "D-###". Must exist in docs/DECISIONS.md; sync renders a
30	#             link line into the managed region and warns about unknown IDs.

57	
58	## A. Hardware and interfaces
59	
60	### A.1 — The Pi reads OBD2 through a USB adapter; raw CAN is a stretch goal ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
61	
62	`D-015` · Decided M1, 2026-09-21 · **By:** Camden + Claude
63	· **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
64	· **Supersedes:** D-001 (§G.1)
65	
66	**Decision.** A USB OBD2 adapter with an ELM327-compatible chip plugs into the OBD2 port
67	and appears on the Pi as a serial device, pinned to `/dev/obd` by a udev rule. Our C daemon
68	sends Mode 01 requests over it and parses the replies. Prefer an STN-chip adapter (e.g.
69	OBDLink SX) over a clone ELM327. No MCP2515, no SPI, no CAN wiring.
70	
71	**Raw CAN is a stretch goal** — an MCP2515 on SPI, taken up only after mechanisms D and E
72	are implemented *and measured*.
73	
74	**Why.** Camden's call (PROMPTLOG E-02): time spent making raw CAN access work was time
75	not spent on the problem. The adapter speaks every OBD2 protocol for us, which is exactly
76	what a plug-in product (D-011) needs, and it removes a class of hardware risk — 5 V on
77	MISO, crystal frequency, bus termination — that could kill a Pi or disturb a daily
78	driver's bus.
79	
80	**Cost — the reason D-001 existed, still true.** An adapter hands us parsed ASCII at
81	roughly 10–20 PID replies per second, with no interrupt line and no bus timing. That
82	takes most of the mechanism menu away from the OBD data path; **D-017** records what
83	survives. Clone ELM327s are also unreliable (truncated buffers, fake firmware), which is
84	why the STN chip is preferred.
85	
86	**Consequences.** The capture daemon becomes a serial reader. Wiring, BOM, provisioning
87	and the design doc follow. The PID survey needs no extra hardware — the same adapter does
88	it.
89

272	## B. Systems architecture and mechanisms
273	
274	### B.1 — Mechanism commitments: D and E; B and F only with a Pi-side sensor ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
275	
276	`D-017` · Decided M1, 2026-09-21 · **By:** Camden + Claude
277	· **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
278	· **Supersedes:** D-002 (§G.3)
279	
280	The handout requires two, implemented by us and measured.
281	
282	| Mechanism | Status | Where |
283	| --- | --- | --- |
284	| **D** — custom append-only storage, crash-consistent | **committed** | `src/store/` |
285	| **E** — multi-process with a supervisor | **committed** | `src/supervisor/`, `src/ipc/` |
286	| **B** — interrupt-driven input with a polling comparison | only if `pisensor` adds an MPU-6050 | capture path for that sensor |
287	| **F** — high-rate no-drop SPSC ring | only if `pisensor` adds an MPU-6050 | `src/ipc/ring.c` |
288	| **A**, **C**, raw CAN | stretch, after D and E are measured | — |
289	
290	**D.** *The defining constraint: power is cut mid-write every time the key turns off*
291	(D-011). We never get a clean shutdown. Measured by pulling power mid-write, repeatedly,
292	and proving recovery (`expcrash`).
293	
294	**E.** A recorder that dies silently has actively harmed its user, who believes it is on
295	duty. Any child may be `kill -9`'d; the system degrades, logs, recovers. Measured by killing
296	each child repeatedly and timing detection and recovery (`expkill`).
297	
298	**Why B and F left the OBD data path (D-015).** B needs an interrupt that *our* design
299	services. The USB adapter's interrupts belong to the kernel's USB-serial driver; our process
300	only blocks on a tty, and at ~10–20 replies/s a poll loop keeps up trivially — the
301	comparison would measure the tty layer, not a design of ours. F needs a *high-rate* stream;
302	~10–20 samples/s never stresses a ring, so "zero drops under contention" would be true and
303	meaningless.
304	
305	**What brings them back.** An MPU-6050 on the Pi's I2C, its `INT` pin on a GPIO: kHz
306	samples from a hardware FIFO give a real interrupt-vs-polling comparison (B) and a rate
307	that stresses the ring (F). That is board item `pisensor`, due at M2.
308	
309	**The ring stays regardless.** It is how capture hands samples to storage across the
310	process boundary E requires, and B.3 still binds it.
311	
312	**Risk.** D and E alone meet the floor exactly. If either measurement fails, nothing is in
313	reserve — which is why `pisensor` is on the critical path.
314	
315	### B.2 — Four processes, not one 🔒
316	
317	`D-002` (corollary) · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
318	
319	`obdd`, `storaged`, `analyzed` and `supervisor` are separate processes with separate
320	address spaces, communicating over a shared-memory ring and Unix domain sockets.
321	
322	**Why.** Fault isolation is the product requirement, not an architectural preference: the
323	analysis engine is the most complex and least trustworthy component, and it must not be
324	able to take the capture path down with it. One process would be simpler and would fail
325	the thing the device exists to do.
326	
327	### B.3 — The ring refuses rather than overwrites 🔒
328	
329	Decided M0 · **By:** Claude, from D-002 · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
330	
331	When the ring is full the producer returns failure and increments an overrun counter. It
332	does **not** overwrite the oldest unread slot.
333	
334	**Why.** Overwriting loses data silently, and silent loss is the exact failure mechanism F
335	exists to make impossible. A refusal is visible, countable, and reportable; an overwrite
336	looks like a quiet minute. Enforced by `tests/test_ring.c`.
337	
338	**Reviewer note.** This is a real trade: under sustained overload we drop *new* data
339	rather than *old*. If that is ever the wrong choice for a diagnostic, reopen this.

376	### B.5 — One warning light, driven by the supervisor ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
377	
378	`D-014` · Decided M1, 2026-09-21 · **By:** Camden + Claude
379	· **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
380	
381	**Decision.** One LED on a GPIO (proposed GPIO17, header pin 11, through 330 Ω), written
382	**only by the supervisor**. Every state in which the device is working is a *blink
383	pattern*:
384	
385	| Light | Meaning | Priority |
386	| --- | --- | --- |
387	| fast blink (~4 Hz) | **degraded** — a child is down, the adapter silent while the engine runs, storage failing, or undervoltage | highest |
388	| double-blink, pause | **a verdict has surfaced** (after D.3 hysteresis and dwell) — look at the phone | |
389	| slow blink (~1 Hz) | on duty, recording, nothing to report | lowest |
390	| **steady on or steady off** | **the device is not running.** Never a valid state. | — |
391	
392	**Why a light at all.** The 3 a.m. test: nobody is looking at a phone at the moment that
393	matters. It also makes "honest reporting through our own interface" (demo movement 1)
394	visible from across the room when a sensor is unplugged.
395	
396	**Why every live state blinks.** A GPIO keeps its last level after the process driving it
397	dies. If "verdict" were solid-on, a crashed supervisor would freeze the light into a false
398	alarm, or into a false all-clear if it froze off. With blink-only states, a stuck light of
399	either kind can only mean *not running*. This is mechanism E's principle — a recorder that
400	dies silently has harmed its user — applied to the one output a driver actually sees.
401	
402	**Why the supervisor, not `analyzed`.** The supervisor already knows every child's
403	liveness (mechanism E), so it can show "degraded" when `analyzed` itself has died; a light
404	owned by `analyzed` would show a stale verdict instead. Verdicts reach the supervisor over
405	the existing UDS. One writer, no GPIO contention.
406	
407	**Cost.** One more thing the supervisor does, and one more thing it must not block on: the
408	blink timer must never delay `waitpid` handling. Color, brightness and placement are open
409	(M4 enclosure).

413	## C. Storage and data integrity
414	
415	### C.1 — Append-only, self-framing, CRC'd records 🔒
416	
417	`D-002/D` · Decided M0 · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
418	
419	Records are never rewritten in place. Each carries a magic number for resynchronization
420	and a CRC32 over its whole body. Recovery scans from the last known-good offset, verifies
421	CRCs, truncates the torn tail, and logs exactly what was lost.
422	
423	**Why.** We are interrupted mid-write by design, several times a day. Rewriting in place
424	can destroy data that was previously correct; appending can only ever damage the last
425	record. The CRC is what makes a torn record *detectable* rather than merely wrong — and
426	wrong numbers you trust are more dangerous than missing numbers you know about.
427	
428	**Open sub-decision (M2, Lance):** fsync batch size and interval. There is no correct
429	value, only one justifiable from user requirements. Document the argument in `docs/DESIGN.md`
430	§4 before writing the code.
431	
432	### C.2 — Every record carries a provenance tag 🔒
433	
434	Decided M0 · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
435	
436	Every record and every log line carries `src = live | replay | synth`. Present in the
437	format from day one, before any replay tooling exists.
438	
439	**Why.** Handout §5: replayed or synthesized data must be labeled everywhere it appears —
440	logs, report, demo. Making it a mandatory field rather than a convention means it is
441	structurally impossible to forget. Mislabeling synthesized data as live is the single
442	integrity failure this course is best equipped to detect, and the worst trade available
443	anywhere in it.

447	## D. Intelligence and analysis
448	
449	### D.1 — Self-trained model; training in Python, inference in C 🔒
450	
451	`D-004` · Decided M0 · **By:** Camden (confirmed with instructor)
452	· **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
453	
454	A locally-trained, self-authored model is permitted; hosted APIs and third-party
455	pretrained weights are not. Therefore: training in `tools/train/`, weights versioned under
456	`models/` with the training commit in the header, **inference in C in `src/analysis/`**, no
457	network at runtime.
458	
459	**Why inference in C.** First and most important for the grade: the runtime path sits
460	inside the supervised multi-process architecture, and a Python process there muddies the
461	boundary a grader must verify in sixty seconds. Second: it removes an interpreter, a
462	garbage collector and ~30 MB of RSS from a 48-hour memory-stability test we are graded on.
463	
464	**What the model is not doing.** The features are the intelligence — operating-point
465	binning, per-bin baselines, Mahalanobis residuals, Theil–Sen trends, all hand-written.
466	Delete the weights file and the system still produces residuals and trends; it loses only
467	the final labeling step. That separation is deliberate and it is the answer at the defense.
468	
469	### D.2 — Analysis pipeline shape 🔒
470	
471	Decided M0 · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
472	
473	Operating-point binning (RPM × load × coolant temp) → per-bin running mean/variance →
474	multivariate residual (Mahalanobis) → robust trend (Theil–Sen) → classifier → state
475	machine with hysteresis and dwell.
476	
477	**Why binning comes first.** Comparing a cold idle to a warm cruise is a false-alarm
478	generator. Every comparison happens inside one bin, against genuinely comparable
479	conditions. This single step removes more false positives than anything else downstream.
480	
481	**Why multivariate.** The signal is the *correlation between sensors*, not any single
482	sensor's value — oil pressure is supposed to rise with RPM. A measure of anomaly that
483	already accounts for normal partnerships, and alarms only when a partnership breaks, is
484	what makes this something a threshold provably cannot do (handout §3.3).
485	
486	### D.3 — Hysteresis and dwell before any verdict surfaces 🔒
487	
488	Decided M0 · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
489	
490	No verdict reaches the user until it has persisted. Trip and un-trip levels differ
491	deliberately.
492	
493	**Why.** A monitor that cries wolf twice gets unplugged, and an unplugged monitor is worse
494	than none because someone far away believes it is on duty. **False-positive rate is a
495	first-class metric in `docs/EVALUATION.md`, not an afterthought.**
496	
497	### D.4 — The threshold test, as a standing rule 🔒
498	
499	Decided M0 · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
500	
501	Every diagnostic we ship must require at least two cooperating sensors to reach its
502	conclusion. If a single threshold on a single value could produce the verdict, it is not
503	intelligence and it does not count. **Write the reason down in `docs/DESIGN.md` when
504	adding a diagnostic** — this is checked at the defense.

511	
512	`D-003` · Decided M0 · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
513	
514	The claim we defend is: *"detects the three faults we can induce on this vehicle, with
515	these error rates."* Not "predicts failure." Not "generalizes to any post-1996 car."
516	*(Narrowed from "these two vehicles" by D-016, 2026-09-21.)*
517	
518	1. **Oil pressure degradation across oil life** — residual after normalizing for RPM and
519	   temperature, trended across an interval.
520	2. **Cooling system anomaly** — thermostat short-cycling signature (period and amplitude)
521	   and abnormal warm-up slope, gated on ambient temp and load.
522	3. **Mixture drift** — long-term fuel trim divergence as a function of load.
523	
524	**Why.** Handout §5 says it directly: a narrow claim met and measured outscores a broad
525	claim gestured at. Twelve vague diagnoses is the named failure mode for this project's
526	seed.

529	
530	`D-003` (corollary) · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
531	
532	We cannot wait a semester for a failure, so we provoke conditions and label the recordings:
533	
534	- **Vacuum leak** — briefly disconnect a small vacuum line. Reversible, safe, moves LTFT
535	  within a minute.
536	- **Cooling** — partially block radiator airflow with cardboard.
537	- **Sensor fault** — unplug a sensor. Also demo day's injected fault, so it gets rehearsed.
538	- **Oil** — log continuously across a real oil change on the CR-V. Cannot be faked
539	  and cannot be rushed, which is why baseline collection starts at M2.
540	
541	Ten labeled recordings we made beat ten thousand unlabeled samples we found, because we
542	know what ours mean — and we will be asked at the defense how we know.

544	### E.3 — 48-hour soak: live sensors vs. a fake OBD2 port ❓ OPEN
545	
546	`D-006` · **Owner:** Camden · **Tracked as:** board item `soakq` (label `decision`)
547	· **Must close before M4** · Blocks nothing before M3
548	
549	**The conflict.** A car cannot run for 48 hours, so Camden's memo (PROBLEM.md, risk)
550	proposes a **fake OBD2 port** that answers Mode 01 requests continuously — board item
551	`obdsim`. Handout §5 endorses exactly this kind of harness as "a legitimate systems
552	artifact." But the same paragraph says: *"The 48-hour soak and the live demonstration run
553	on live sensors; everything else may run on honest replay."* A soak on the fake port is
554	synthesized data by definition, and is labeled `src=synth` everywhere regardless.
555	
556	**Options.**
557	
558	- **(a)** A written exception from Pallickara for a soak on the fake port. The email text
559	  is in the body of board item `soakq`.
560	- **(b)** A sensor on the Pi itself (`pisensor`: MPU-6050 and/or DS18B20, ~$8) runs live
561	  for all 48 hours while the OBD side comes from the fake port, labeled `synth`.
562	- **(c)** The parked CR-V, key in accessory, on the live port with a battery tender. Fully
563	  live, but engine-off values barely move, the socket must stay live in accessory (D-011),
564	  and it ties up Lance's car for two days.
565	
566	**Posture.** Build as if (a) is refused. (b) is the default fallback, which is one more
567	reason `pisensor` is on the critical path. The `src=` field is in the record format
568	regardless.
569	
570	---
571	
572	## F. Process, team and tooling
573	
574	### F.1 — Git and pull-request law 🔒
575	
576	Decided M0 · **By:** Camden · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
577	
578	The binding ruleset lives in **`CLAUDE.md` §7**, because that is the file the agent reads
579	every session. Summary of the load-bearing parts:
580	
581	- Claude never commits to `main`, never merges, never force-pushes, never `git add -A`.
582	- One commit = one responsibility, sized by what it is responsible for — not by line
583	  count. *(The original ≤ 150-line / ≤ 3-file and ≤ 500-line PR caps were replaced by the
584	  responsibility test in `CLAUDE.md` §7.3 and §7.5 during M0; CLAUDE.md is the binding
585	  text.)*
586	- One PR = one reviewable claim.
587	- **If the reviewer does not understand a line, the PR does not merge.** The remedy is
588	  explanation or a smaller commit, never trust.
589	- Every commit builds and passes tests on its own.
590	
591	**Why so strict.** Our process grade is computed from transcripts corroborated against
592	commits, the git history is a graded deliverable, and neither of us will break down a
593	thousand-line diff. A commit small enough to review in ninety seconds is a commit we will
594	actually review — and the defense asks us to answer for individual lines.
595	
596	### F.2 — Ownership map 🔒
597	
598	Decided M0 · **By:** Camden · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
599	
600	| Owner | Subsystems |
601	| --- | --- |
602	| **Camden** | `src/obd/`, `src/ipc/` |
603	| **Lance** | `src/store/`, `src/analysis/`, `tools/train/` |
604	| **Shared** | `src/supervisor/`, `src/interface/`, `src/common/`, build, docs |
605	
606	Ownership means **first authorship and answerability at the defense**, not exclusivity.
607	Each partner must still be able to answer one question from across the boundary — demo day
608	guarantees one.
609	
610	### F.3 — Milestone dates ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
611	
612	`D-008` · **Owner:** Camden · **Tracked as:** board item `dates` (label `question`)
613	· **Answered:** 2026-09-21, by Camden · **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜
614	
615	**Answer.** Camden verified the milestone dates against the syllabus (checked off in
616	`docs/milestones.md`, 2026-09-21): the `[[milestone]]` dates in `docs/board.toml` stand as
617	written, M0 2026-09-20 through M6 2026-12-18. Recorded by Claude from that check-off;
618	Camden marks it LOCKED in his own commit.
619	
620	**Why it mattered.** The handout gives weeks, not dates; a one-week error would have moved
621	the M4 soak start, and M4 already lands on Thanksgiving week.
622	
623	### F.4 — Markdown is linted with markdownlint, at a 90-column wrap ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
624	
625	`D-018` · **By:** Claude, in Camden's session 2026-09-23
626	· **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜
627	
628	`.markdownlint.jsonc` at the repository root sets the rules the VS Code markdownlint
629	extension enforces: every default rule on, lines wrapped at **90 columns** (tables, code
630	and headings exempt), `<details>`, `<summary>`, `<code>`, `<sub>` and `<br>` allowed as
631	inline HTML, and tables in the compact `| a | b |` / `| --- | --- |` style.
632	`.markdownlintignore` excludes `docs/handout/`, which is a transcription of the
633	instructor's PDF.
634	
635	Spelling is **American English**, checked by the VS Code Code Spell Checker (cSpell).
636	`cspell.json` holds the project dictionary: our jargon, command names and board slugs.
637	Add a word there when it is a real term; fix it when it is a typo.
638	
639	**Why 90, not the default 80.** The docs were already wrapped at about 90: at 80 the repo
640	raised 1,184 line-length warnings, and at 90 it raised 24. Rewrapping everything to 80
641	would bury every file's history in reflow for no reader benefit.
642	
643	**Why a config at all.** Without one, each editor shows over 1,500 warnings, and a real
644	problem (a broken heading tree, a list that does not render) is invisible in the noise.
645	
646	---
647	
648	## G. Superseded
649	
650	When a decision is replaced, it moves here with a pointer to its replacement. Never delete
651	one: the reasoning is evidence, and "what M2 got wrong" is a graded section of
652	`docs/DESIGN.md`.
653	
654	### G.1 — (was A.1) CAN reaches the Pi via MCP2515 on SPI, not Bluetooth 🗑
655	
656	`D-001` · Decided M0 · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
657	· **Superseded 2026-09-21 by D-015 (§A.1)** — raw CAN became a stretch goal.
658	
659	**Decision.** The Pi reads raw CAN frames through an MCP2515 + TJA1050 module on SPI0,
660	with the controller's `INT` line on a GPIO for edge-triggered receive. Not a Bluetooth
661	ELM327 dongle.
662	
663	**Why.** A Bluetooth ELM327 hands us parsed ASCII over a userspace socket at a few
664	samples per second. With no interrupt line, no SPI transaction and no bus-level timing,
665	mechanisms **A, B, C and F all become unavailable** — and the handout requires at least
666	two mechanisms implemented by us, below the application layer. The MCP2515 path keeps
667	the kernel boundary inside our repository, where it is graded. It is also better for the
668	user: raw bus access sees frames the ELM327 protocol never exposes, at the rate the ECU
669	publishes them rather than the rate a request/response dongle can poll.
670	
671	**Cost.** More wiring, a 3.3 V/5 V level question to get right, one-time decode work per
672	vehicle. Accepted.
673	
674	**What replaced it, and what that cost.** D-015 accepts the mechanism loss this entry
675	warned about, in exchange for hardware that works on day one; D-017 records which
676	mechanisms survive.
677	
678	### G.2 — (was A.2) Testbeds: Subaru Outback and Lance's Honda 🗑
679	
680	`D-005` · Decided M0 · **By:** Camden · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
681	· **Superseded 2026-09-21 by D-016 (§A.2)** — the second vehicle was cut, as this entry
682	said it would be first.
683	
684	**Decision.** Two daily-driven vehicles — Camden's Subaru Outback and Lance's Honda.
685	
686	**Why.** The product's thesis is that a generic maintenance interval is a generalization
687	and your car is not generic. One vehicle cannot demonstrate that; two with different duty
688	cycles can, and the comparison is the demo's strongest five seconds. Two also gives each
689	partner a vehicle they can instrument on their own schedule.
690	
691	**Cost.** Roughly doubles decode and baseline-collection work, and the baseline window is
692	the one thing that cannot be compressed by working harder in Week 14. Mitigation: start
693	on standard Mode 01 PIDs only; manufacturer-specific frames are a stretch.
694	
695	**Risk.** If the schedule slips, the **first** thing cut is the second vehicle — not a
696	mechanism, and not the evaluation. Record it here if it happens.
697	
698	### G.3 — (was B.1) Mechanism commitments: B, D, E, F 🗑
699	
700	`D-002` · Decided M0 · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
701	· **Superseded 2026-09-21 by D-017 (§B.1)** — with raw CAN a stretch goal (D-015), B and F
702	lost their data source.
703	
704	The handout requires two. We commit four and will measure all of them.
705	
706	**B — interrupt-driven input with a polling comparison.** `src/can/`. At 500 kbit/s a busy
707	bus delivers a frame roughly every 230 µs; the MCP2515's two receive buffers overflow in
708	milliseconds. A poll loop either burns a core or drops frames. Measured as event-latency
709	distribution and CPU, both ways, idle and loaded.
710	
711	**D — custom append-only storage, crash-consistent.** `src/store/`. *The defining
712	constraint: power is cut mid-write every time the key turns off.* We never get a clean
713	shutdown. Measured by pulling power mid-write, repeatedly, and proving recovery.
714	
715	**E — multi-process with a supervisor.** `src/supervisor/`, `src/ipc/`. A recorder that
716	dies silently has actively harmed its user, who believes it is on duty. Any child may be
717	`kill -9`'d; the system degrades, logs, recovers.
718	
719	**F — no-drop SPSC ring, sequence-accounted.** `src/ipc/ring.c`. Key-on produces a burst;
720	a gap in the record is a gap in the diagnosis. Measured as sustained rate with zero drops
721	under contention.
722	
723	**Stretch, M4+ only:** **A** (character driver for the MCP2515) and **C** (`SCHED_FIFO` on
724	the capture path). Do not start either until B, D, E and F are implemented *and measured*.
725	A half-finished kernel module is worth zero points and costs two weeks.
726	
727	---
728	
729	## Adding a decision
730	
731	Append it to the right category with the next free `D-###` for citation, and fill every
732	field. If Claude made it without a human present, it is ⚠️ **UNREVIEWED** and it goes in the
733	Review Queue at the top — **in the same commit that implements it**, never a later one.
734	
735	**Closing an open question.** When a human answers a `decision` or `question` issue, the
736	answer moves here as a 🔒 LOCKED entry citing the issue number, and the issue closes. One
737	commit does both — resolving one question is one responsibility, however many lines it
738	touches across this file (`CLAUDE.md` §7.3, documentation rules).

---

## A. Hardware and interfaces

### A.1 — The Pi reads OBD2 through a USB adapter; raw CAN is a stretch goal ⚠️ UNREVIEWED

`D-015` · Decided M1, 2026-09-21 · **By:** Camden + Claude
· **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
· **Supersedes:** D-001 (§G.1)

**Decision.** A USB OBD2 adapter with an ELM327-compatible chip plugs into the OBD2 port
and appears on the Pi as a serial device, pinned to `/dev/obd` by a udev rule. Our C daemon
sends Mode 01 requests over it and parses the replies. Prefer an STN-chip adapter (e.g.
OBDLink SX) over a clone ELM327. No MCP2515, no SPI, no CAN wiring.

**Raw CAN is a stretch goal** — an MCP2515 on SPI, taken up only after mechanisms D and E
are implemented *and measured*.

**Why.** Camden's call (PROMPTLOG E-02): time spent making raw CAN access work was time
not spent on the problem. The adapter speaks every OBD2 protocol for us, which is exactly
what a plug-in product (D-011) needs, and it removes a class of hardware risk — 5 V on
MISO, crystal frequency, bus termination — that could kill a Pi or disturb a daily
driver's bus.

**Cost — the reason D-001 existed, still true.** An adapter hands us parsed ASCII at
roughly 10–20 PID replies per second, with no interrupt line and no bus timing. That
takes most of the mechanism menu away from the OBD data path; **D-017** records what
survives. Clone ELM327s are also unreliable (truncated buffers, fake firmware), which is
why the STN chip is preferred.

**Consequences.** The capture daemon becomes a serial reader. Wiring, BOM, provisioning
and the design doc follow. The PID survey needs no extra hardware — the same adapter does
it.

### A.2 — One testbed: Lance's 2015 Honda CR-V EX-L ⚠️ UNREVIEWED

`D-016` · Decided M1, 2026-09-21 · **By:** Camden + Claude
· **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
· **Supersedes:** D-005 (§G.2)

**Decision.** The CR-V is the only testbed. The Subaru Outback is dropped.

**Why.** Camden's call, 2026-09-21. D-005 itself named the second vehicle as the first
thing to cut when the schedule slipped, and the CAN detour (PROMPTLOG E-02) spent that
slack. One car halves the survey, baseline and ground-truth work, and the baseline window
is the one thing that cannot be compressed by working harder in Week 14.

**Cost.**

- The two-car contrast — *"the same sticker says 5,000 miles to both cars, and the cars
  disagree"* — was the thesis's strongest demonstration, and it is gone. The thesis is now
  argued within one car: its measured condition against its own sticker and its own
  Maintenance Minder estimate (D-007).
- If the CR-V publishes only an oil-pressure switch, diagnostic #1 has no second car to
  fall back on (`oilq`).
- Every live capture, induced fault and soak on real data runs on Lance's car and Lance's
  schedule; Camden owns the capture code but not the car.

### A.3 — Honda year/model/engine ⚠️ UNREVIEWED

`D-007` · **Owner:** Lance · **Tracked as:** GitHub issue `honda` (label `question`)
· **Answered:** 2026-09-21, by Camden in session · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
· **Blocks:** the PID survey, and therefore diagnostic #1

**Answer.** **2015 Honda CR-V EX-L.** By model year that is the 2015 refresh: 2.4 L
direct-injected four-cylinder (K24W) with a CVT. FWD or AWD is not yet recorded. The
engine and transmission are inferred from the model year, not read off the car — Lance
confirms against the VIN or the door-jamb sticker, then closes the issue.

**What the answer changes.**

- **No Honda Sensing on the EX-L** (it was Touring-only in 2015), so there is no
  lane-keep camera connector to tap. The OBD2 port is the tap point (**D-011**).
- **Oil pressure is expected to be a switch, not a sender.** This is inference from
  Honda practice, not a service-manual reading; `pidhonda` confirms it. If true, diagnostic
  #1 cannot run from any tap point and must be replaced or dropped (`oilq`).
- **The Honda has Maintenance Minder** — an oil-life percentage estimated from how the
  engine has been run. For this car the "generic 5,000-mile sticker" framing is false, and
  `docs/PROBLEM.md` must answer the skeptic's version instead: *the car already estimates
  this.* The answer is that the Minder is an open-loop estimate from a usage model; it
  never measures the engine's condition. Ours measures.

We still need, from the car itself: which Mode 01 PIDs the ECU actually supports, and
whether oil pressure is published as an analog value or only as an idiot-light bit.

**Why it is urgent.** A large fraction of consumer vehicles publish only a binary
low-oil-pressure switch. If the CR-V does not publish analog oil pressure, **diagnostic #1
is not implementable from the port** and we must substitute a physical sender (real
automotive work on a daily driver) or replace the diagnostic. This is the project's named
risk in `docs/PROBLEM.md`.

**Action.** Run a supported-PID scan on the CR-V with the USB OBD2 adapter (D-015) —
a ten-minute experiment. Record in `docs/hardware/pid-survey.md`.

### A.4 — Capture the schematic in KiCad; do not fabricate a PCB 🔒

`D-009` · Decided M0 · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜

**Decision.** We draw the full schematic in KiCad (`electricalDrawing/`, KiCad 10, owned
by Lance) and treat it as the source of truth for wiring and the BOM. We do **not**
fabricate a custom PCB unless we take The Reach (handout §14). The empty `.kicad_pcb`
stays in the repo on purpose.

**Why.** A custom board earns zero points — the rubric grades mechanisms, measurements and
the soak — and fab turnaround lands on top of critical path B, already the likeliest cause
of an M2 slip. A breadboard plus an off-the-shelf MCP2515 module clears every guardrail, and
the handout is explicit that a food container is an acceptable enclosure.

**Why the schematic is still worth the hours.** Three graded artifacts depend on it:
`docs/DESIGN.md` needs a defensible wiring story; `docs/hardware/wiring.md` needs pin assignments
that cannot drift from the build; and the three-isolated-workers test needs a parts-only
buyer who can order from the BOM without seeing the design. A hand-maintained pin table will
disagree with reality by Week 9. A generated one cannot.

**Consequences.** `make hwcheck` (ERC) and `make hwdocs` (SVG, BOM, netlist) enter the
build. `docs/hardware/wiring.md` and `BOM.md` become **derived** artifacts. `CLAUDE.md`
§7.12 requires a rendered schematic in any PR touching hardware.

### A.5 — ERC is a build failure, and the schematic SVG is committed 🔒

`D-010` · Decided M0 · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜

**Decision.** `kicad-cli sch erc --exit-code-violations` runs as `make hwcheck`; violations
fail the build. `make hwdocs` renders the schematic to `docs/figures/electricalDrawing.svg`,
and that SVG is **committed**.

**Why the ERC gate.** It makes electrical correctness the same kind of object as
`-Wall -Wextra -Werror`: a machine-checked precondition rather than a thing someone
remembers to look at. Unconnected pins and power-output conflicts are exactly the class of
error that survives a human read and kills a board.

**Why commit a generated file.** Normally we would not. But a reviewer cannot read a diff
of S-expression coordinates, and §7.6 says a PR nobody understands does not merge — so
without a rendered picture, hardware would fall outside the review process entirely. The
SVG is the diff a human can actually read. It is regenerated, never hand-edited.

**Open sub-item (Lance, M2):** `sym-lib-table` referenced `CS370_Project_Library.kicad_sym`,
which did not exist — KiCad errors on project open. An empty library is committed to resolve
it; populate it as parts are drawn.

### A.6 — Plug-in form: OBD2 port for data, car USB-C for power ⚠️ UNREVIEWED

`D-011` · Decided M1, 2026-09-21 · **By:** Camden + Claude
· **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜

*Data half revised 2026-09-21 by D-015, before any review: the MCP2515 and Y-splitter
became a USB OBD2 adapter.*

**Decision.** The device is a box anyone could install without tools:

- **Data:** the USB OBD2 adapter (D-015) plugs into the OBD2 port; one USB cable runs to
  the Pi.
- **Power:** the car's own USB-C port, or a USB-C adapter in the 12 V socket, into the Pi.
  No buck converter.
- **Nothing is cut, spliced, pierced or clamped** on the car.

**Why.** The product thesis is that this is a thing an ordinary owner plugs in, so the
prototype is built the way the product would be installed. We are building the model to
prove the idea is worth something, not the finished product — but a prototype that needs
harness surgery proves a different, less interesting idea. Switched USB power also means
no battery drain while parked, and it makes mechanism D's defining constraint literally
true: power is cut, unannounced, at every key-off.

**Alternatives rejected** (discussed 2026-09-21): splicing the bus behind the OBD2 port
(the same conductors as the port pins, plus a cut harness on a daily driver); an in-line
harness at the forward camera (the 2015 CR-V EX-L has none, D-007); a contactless bus
clamp (receive-only, a black box); powering the Pi from OBD2 pin 16 through our own buck
converter (live with the key off, and more hardware to build and defend).

**Rule this imposes:** **the Pi must not brown out at crank.** The USB-C supply is rated
≥ 5.1 V / 3 A (Pi 4), and is proven by `vcgencmd get_throttled` after a cold start, not
by its label (`docs/hardware/wiring.md`).

**Cost.**

- No recording while the key is off — nothing happens then worth recording, but the device
  also cannot run overnight in a parked car.
- **The OBD2 adapter itself draws from pin 16, which is live with the key off.** Its
  key-off current must be measured before it is left plugged in overnight.
- D-006 option (c), the parked-car soak, now requires a socket that stays live in
  accessory plus a battery tender.
- The product is "one box, two cables", not "one dongle".

### A.7 — Standard Mode 01 requests are the primary data path ⚠️ UNREVIEWED

`D-012` · Decided M1, 2026-09-21 · **By:** Camden + Claude
· **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜

*Revised 2026-09-21 by D-015, before any review: the CAN-level detail (arbitration IDs,
broadcast frames, a listen-only flag, the port-traffic check) went with the MCP2515.*

**Decision.** The capture daemon gets its signals by sending **standard OBD2 Mode 01
requests** through the USB adapter (D-015) on a fixed, rate-limited, round-robin schedule,
one request outstanding at a time. Every timeout and every unanswered PID is logged.

**Why.** D-011 makes this a plug-in device, and the thing that makes a plug-in device work
on a car it has never seen is the part of the protocol every car must speak: Mode 01 is
mandatory on US cars from model year 1996. *"Learns this car's normal"* is precisely what
lets one device serve different cars without per-model decode work: it never needs to
know what normal *is* ahead of time.

**Sample-rate consequence.** Signals are round-robined, so each PID is sampled at
(request rate ÷ PID count) — on the order of 1 Hz each for a ~10 requests/s budget over
~8 PIDs. That is ample for what we diagnose (oil trend over weeks, warm-up over minutes,
fuel trim against load) and must be stated in `docs/DESIGN.md` §4. The request budget itself
is a design-doc number to justify, not a constant to pick.

**Cost.** The device sends requests to the car's ECU. Kept safe by the rate limit, one
outstanding request, and only standard read-only Mode 01 requests — the same thing every
scan tool does.

**Scope note.** "Works on any car" is the product's direction, not our claim. The claim is
still E.1: three faults, one car, measured error rates.

---

## B. Systems architecture and mechanisms

### B.1 — Mechanism commitments: D and E; B and F only with a Pi-side sensor ⚠️ UNREVIEWED

`D-017` · Decided M1, 2026-09-21 · **By:** Camden + Claude
· **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
· **Supersedes:** D-002 (§G.3)

The handout requires two, implemented by us and measured.

| Mechanism | Status | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **D** — custom append-only storage, crash-consistent | **committed** | `src/store/` |
| **E** — multi-process with a supervisor | **committed** | `src/supervisor/`, `src/ipc/` |
| **B** — interrupt-driven input with a polling comparison | only if `pisensor` adds an MPU-6050 | capture path for that sensor |
| **F** — high-rate no-drop SPSC ring | only if `pisensor` adds an MPU-6050 | `src/ipc/ring.c` |
| **A**, **C**, raw CAN | stretch, after D and E are measured | — |

**D.** *The defining constraint: power is cut mid-write every time the key turns off*
(D-011). We never get a clean shutdown. Measured by pulling power mid-write, repeatedly,
and proving recovery (`expcrash`).

**E.** A recorder that dies silently has actively harmed its user, who believes it is on
duty. Any child may be `kill -9`'d; the system degrades, logs, recovers. Measured by killing
each child repeatedly and timing detection and recovery (`expkill`).

**Why B and F left the OBD data path (D-015).** B needs an interrupt that *our* design
services. The USB adapter's interrupts belong to the kernel's USB-serial driver; our process
only blocks on a tty, and at ~10–20 replies/s a poll loop keeps up trivially — the
comparison would measure the tty layer, not a design of ours. F needs a *high-rate* stream;
~10–20 samples/s never stresses a ring, so "zero drops under contention" would be true and
meaningless.

**What brings them back.** An MPU-6050 on the Pi's I2C, its `INT` pin on a GPIO: kHz
samples from a hardware FIFO give a real interrupt-vs-polling comparison (B) and a rate
that stresses the ring (F). That is board item `pisensor`, due at M2.

**The ring stays regardless.** It is how capture hands samples to storage across the
process boundary E requires, and B.3 still binds it.

**Risk.** D and E alone meet the floor exactly. If either measurement fails, nothing is in
reserve — which is why `pisensor` is on the critical path.

### B.2 — Four processes, not one 🔒

`D-002` (corollary) · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜

`obdd`, `storaged`, `analyzed` and `supervisor` are separate processes with separate
address spaces, communicating over a shared-memory ring and Unix domain sockets.

**Why.** Fault isolation is the product requirement, not an architectural preference: the
analysis engine is the most complex and least trustworthy component, and it must not be
able to take the capture path down with it. One process would be simpler and would fail
the thing the device exists to do.

### B.3 — The ring refuses rather than overwrites 🔒

Decided M0 · **By:** Claude, from D-002 · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜

When the ring is full the producer returns failure and increments an overrun counter. It
does **not** overwrite the oldest unread slot.

**Why.** Overwriting loses data silently, and silent loss is the exact failure mechanism F
exists to make impossible. A refusal is visible, countable, and reportable; an overwrite
looks like a quiet minute. Enforced by `tests/test_ring.c`.

**Reviewer note.** This is a real trade: under sustained overload we drop *new* data
rather than *old*. If that is ever the wrong choice for a diagnostic, reopen this.

### B.4 — The phone is a read-only window over the device's own Wi-Fi ⚠️ UNREVIEWED

`D-013` · Decided M1, 2026-09-21 · **By:** Camden + Claude
· **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜

**Decision.** The Pi runs its own Wi-Fi access point — WPA2, a per-device passphrase, **no
upstream connection, no internet**. The owner's phone joins it and opens a status page
served from `src/interface/` by a supervised child process. The page shows exactly two
things — **status** and **current verdicts** — rendered from the same supervisor UDS verbs
`obdctl` uses. It holds no state, runs no analysis, and writes nothing. `obdctl` remains
the primary, exact interface with all five verbs. No app, no account, no cloud, no
Bluetooth pairing.

**Why.** The user is a car owner, not someone with a terminal in the passenger seat, so a
product that can only be read over SSH has no user. The handout permits it directly
("Serving a dashboard on the LAN is fine", §3.3; CLAUDE.md §2.1), and the device keeps
working with no phone present at all. It also sharpens the phone-app test: the Pi is the
part that is awake at every key-on; the phone is only a window onto what it already
recorded.

**Why so thin.** The handout warns: *"Resist the pretty web app. A crisp CLI with five
query verbs and exact semantics is more defensible, and far more extensible at the
live-modification station."* So the page is a view, not a second interface: two screens,
no framework, and no number on it that `obdctl` cannot also produce. Every graded behavior
remains demonstrable through `obdctl` alone.

**Cost.**

- A network listener in the product. It binds only to the AP interface, is read-only, and
  lives only in `src/interface/`, where `make boundary` already allows network symbols.
- One more process in the 48-hour RSS plot, and Wi-Fi radio power on the car's USB port.
- **Open sub-decision (M2, both):** the server's language. C in `src/interface/` keeps an
  interpreter out of the memory-stability test; Python in `ui/` is permitted by CLAUDE.md
  §2.5 but adds ~30 MB RSS to the soak. Recommendation: C, because the page is tiny.

### B.5 — One warning light, driven by the supervisor ⚠️ UNREVIEWED

`D-014` · Decided M1, 2026-09-21 · **By:** Camden + Claude
· **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜

**Decision.** One LED on a GPIO (proposed GPIO17, header pin 11, through 330 Ω), written
**only by the supervisor**. Every state in which the device is working is a *blink
pattern*:

| Light | Meaning | Priority |
| --- | --- | --- |
| fast blink (~4 Hz) | **degraded** — a child is down, the adapter silent while the engine runs, storage failing, or undervoltage | highest |
| double-blink, pause | **a verdict has surfaced** (after D.3 hysteresis and dwell) — look at the phone | |
| slow blink (~1 Hz) | on duty, recording, nothing to report | lowest |
| **steady on or steady off** | **the device is not running.** Never a valid state. | — |

**Why a light at all.** The 3 a.m. test: nobody is looking at a phone at the moment that
matters. It also makes "honest reporting through our own interface" (demo movement 1)
visible from across the room when a sensor is unplugged.

**Why every live state blinks.** A GPIO keeps its last level after the process driving it
dies. If "verdict" were solid-on, a crashed supervisor would freeze the light into a false
alarm, or into a false all-clear if it froze off. With blink-only states, a stuck light of
either kind can only mean *not running*. This is mechanism E's principle — a recorder that
dies silently has harmed its user — applied to the one output a driver actually sees.

**Why the supervisor, not `analyzed`.** The supervisor already knows every child's
liveness (mechanism E), so it can show "degraded" when `analyzed` itself has died; a light
owned by `analyzed` would show a stale verdict instead. Verdicts reach the supervisor over
the existing UDS. One writer, no GPIO contention.

**Cost.** One more thing the supervisor does, and one more thing it must not block on: the
blink timer must never delay `waitpid` handling. Color, brightness and placement are open
(M4 enclosure).
