| PR | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [#107](https://github.com/CamdenThomas/CS370-Term-Project/pull/107) | Fixes `main`: the 8e8c74a merge had broken `board.toml` and `board.lock.json`. Also files board items for this session's work. |
| [#108](https://github.com/CamdenThomas/CS370-Term-Project/pull/108) | PROBLEM.md grammar, spelling and format pass. |
| [#109](https://github.com/CamdenThomas/CS370-Term-Project/pull/109) | Lint and spelling cleanup across the repo (D-018). |
| [#111](https://github.com/CamdenThomas/CS370-Term-Project/pull/111) `[cross]` | The Bluetooth pivot (D-019). |
| [#114](https://github.com/CamdenThomas/CS370-Term-Project/pull/114) | Condensed CLAUDE.md and the reference chain. |

**The Bluetooth pivot (#111):**
- **Decision:** D-019 records the OBDLink LX (Bluetooth Classic serial, not BLE), read by the Pi's built-in radio. It stays `/dev/obd`, so nothing downstream changes. It also answers why §G.1's old objection to Bluetooth no longer applies.
- **Supersedes D-015:** the USB adapter moves to §G.4 with its text kept, as the fallback.
- **Docs, scaffolds and board:** every live doc, the `obdd` and provisioning TODOs, and 11 open board items now describe Bluetooth. `btcoex` (#110) is new; it measures the Wi-Fi hotspot and Bluetooth sharing the Pi's one radio.
- **One change from the plan:** `order` and `bench` were never actually done, so I rewrote them instead of adding duplicate items. No hardware was bought for the old design.

**The condense (#114):**
- **Size:** CLAUDE.md drops from 28.7 KB to 11.7 KB (59%, not the 70% I estimated) because I kept the graded hard constraints and the five absolutes word for word.
- **Section numbers are unchanged**, so every existing reference to them still points to the right place.
- **Where the rest went:** the reasoning moves verbatim to a new `docs/PROCESS.md`, and the board details into `BOARD.md`. `docs/README.md` is now the index that says which document is the authority for each topic. The PR body maps every removed paragraph to its new home.
- **Your oil-pressure edit** to CLAUDE.md is kept as its own commit.

**Needs you or Lance:**
- **Sign the new decisions:** D-019 (your call on Bluetooth) and D-018 (lint rules), both in the DECISIONS.md review queue.
- **Lance should review** `schematic-conventions.md` and the `schcan` item in #111, plus #112 (a LOCKED ownership entry that disagrees with CLAUDE.md) and #113 (KiCad state files that are still tracked).
- **Check the adapter details:** confirm the OBDLink LX price (~$60, marked "verify"), and whether Raspberry Pi OS still includes the `rfcomm` tool.
- **Board cards didn't move:** run `gh auth refresh -s project`, then `python tools/board_sync.py`.
- **Copy out this session's transcript** once you exit, per §0.

Two mistakes along the way: I committed a `board.toml` that didn't parse (a pipe hid the test failure), and I tagged an item with the wrong decision ID. I caught both and amended them before pushing.

content.text:
None of your VS Code extensions have created files in this project, so I didn't change anything. That covers every branch, since the extensions write into the working folder. What I checked:

- **No VS Code files at all:** no `.vscode/` folder, no `*.code-workspace`, and no cache or local-history files from Code Spell Checker, markdownlint or similar extensions. Their settings live in your home directory (`~/.config/Code/`), not in the repo.
- **One extension-style folder, already ignored:** `tools/__pycache__/` (from running the Python tools), covered by `.gitignore` line 9.

I did find two tracked files that shouldn't be in the repo, but they come from **KiCad**, not VS Code:

- **`electricalDrawing/.history`:** KiCad's local-history folder is its own little git repository. So the repo stores it as a broken submodule pointer, with no `.gitmodules` file.
- **`electricalDrawing/electricalDrawing.kicad_prl`:** KiCad's per-user window state.

Both are already in `.gitignore`. They stay tracked because they were committed before those ignore rules existed. Removing them from git (keeping your local copies) is `git rm --cached` on the two paths, which is exactly board item [#113](https://github.com/CamdenThomas/CS370-Term-Project/issues/113). I filed it for Lance because `electricalDrawing/` is his area.

If you want it done now, say so and I'll put it on its own `[cross]` branch that closes #113, so Lance still reviews it. And if you'd like `.vscode/` ignored up front, in case an extension creates it later, that's a one-line addition I can put on the same branch.
what is cspell.json and all the .markdwnlink files in the repo

They're settings files for the two VS Code extensions that were producing your warnings. I added all three this session in [#109](https://github.com/CamdenThomas/CS370-Term-Project/pull/109), so they're only on the `mdlint` branch and the branches built on it, not on `main` yet.

| File | Read by | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.markdownlint.jsonc` | **markdownlint** extension | The markdown style rules. It keeps every default except lines may be 90 characters (the repo was written that way; the default of 80 caused 1,184 warnings), it allows a few HTML tags we use on purpose (`<details>`, `<sub>`…), and it asks for tables written like `\| --- \|`. |
| `.markdownlintignore` | **markdownlint** extension | Files it skips. It contains one entry, `docs/handout/`, because that's the instructor's handout copied in, not ours to reformat. |
| `cspell.json` | **Code Spell Checker** extension | Sets spelling to American English and lists about 145 project words that aren't in the dictionary: `obdctl`, `storaged`, `RFCOMM`, `Mahalanobis`, board slugs and so on. Without it, every one of those shows a squiggle. |

Why they're committed rather than kept as personal settings:

- **Lance gets them too.** Anyone who opens the repo in VS Code sees the same rules and the same zero-warning baseline.
- **They're how I check my writing.** They're what I lint against before committing, which is the "always write without warnings" rule you asked for.

Because they set a style for both of you, I recorded them as decision D-018 in `docs/DECISIONS.md` §F.4. It's marked ⚠️ UNREVIEWED until you or Lance sign it.

They affect nothing else: not the build, the product or any grading script. Only the editor squiggles change. If you'd rather not have them, remove the three files and D-018 from #109 before merging, and the warnings come back.

When a real project word gets flagged as misspelled, add it to the `words` list in `cspell.json`. When it's an actual typo, fix the typo.

     1	# Problem memo — carwatch (Camden Thomas, Lance Baron)
     2	
     3	## The user
     4	
     5	An average car owner who drives to work every day uses a car very differently from someone
     6	who works from home and takes one road trip a year, yet both are handed the same
     7	recommended maintenance schedule.
     8	
     9	That contrast is the thesis: the same oil-change sticker says 5,000 miles to both cars,
    10	and the cars disagree.
    11	
    12	## The problem
    13	
    14	> Observable and costly: what goes wrong, how often, what it costs in money or worry.
    15	
    16	Maintenance intervals are generalizations. The sticker on the windshield knows nothing
    17	about how this engine has actually been run — a commuter that never reaches operating
    18	temperature and a highway car with the same odometer reading have not aged the same way.
    19	The error runs in both directions, and both are expensive: oil changed far earlier than it
    20	needed to be, or an engine run on oil that lost its pressure margin weeks ago.
    21	
    22	The car's own sensors already measure everything needed to tell these cases apart. What is
    23	missing is a device that records that data continuously, learns what normal looks like for
    24	this car, and flags a developing fault before the check-engine light of doom puts its
    25	owner on an hour-long bus ride.
    26	
    27	## Why a device
    28	
    29	> The 3 a.m. test: why must something be physically present and always awake? And why
    30	> doesn't a phone app already solve this?
    31	
    32	The signal is a slow trend across weeks of driving, and it is only interpretable if you
    33	have the cold starts, the short trips, and the long pulls — *all* of them, not the
    34	drives someone remembered to open an app for. A phone app is present for the trips you
    35	thought to instrument, which is a biased sample of exactly the variable being measured.
    36	
    37	The interesting moment is also never the moment anyone is looking: it is the third cold
    38	start of a February week when warm-up took ninety seconds longer than it did in
    39	January. Nobody is holding a phone then. The device is in the car, awake at key-on,
    40	recording before anyone has decided anything is wrong.
    41	
    42	And the data stays in the car. No account, no upload, no fleet telematics company
    43	holding a log of everywhere this person drove.
    44	
    45	## The sensors
    46	
    47	> Which two (or more) and how they **cooperate** rather than coexist.
    48	
    49	The vehicle's own sensors, read via the OBD2 port: oil pressure, coolant temperature,
    50	intake air temperature, MAP, O2 / fuel trims, RPM, and engine load.
    51	
    52	They cooperate because **no one of them means anything alone.** Oil pressure is a
    53	function of RPM and oil temperature; the diagnostic signal is the *residual* after
    54	normalizing for both, which requires all three sensors to reach one conclusion. Fuel
    55	trim is only interpretable against load. Coolant temperature only indicts a thermostat
    56	once ambient temperature and load have been accounted for. Every verdict this device
    57	produces requires at least two sensors to agree on something a single threshold cannot
    58	see.
    59	
    60	## The mechanisms
    61	
    62	> First guess at two menu items, one sentence of justification each. May change by M2.
    63	
    64	**D — custom append-only storage with crash consistency.** The power is cut mid-write
    65	every single time the key turns off, so the storage layer never gets a clean shutdown
    66	and must recover a torn tail on every boot.
    67	
    68	**E — multi-process architecture with a supervisor.** A recorder that dies silently has
    69	harmed its owner, who believes it is on duty; capture, storage, and analysis run as
    70	separate processes so that a crash in the analysis cannot take the recording down with it.
    71	
    72	## The risk
    73	
    74	The primary risk, named honestly: the oil-life trend needs a real oil interval to develop,
    75	and that is calendar time we cannot buy back by working harder in Week 14. Baseline
    76	collection starts at M2 or it does not happen.
    77	
    78	The second risk is the OBD2 protocol itself. Each manufacturer implements it differently,
    79	across four different *data frames*, and even once those are handled, a received signal
    80	may be impossible to decode because the manufacturer keeps its meaning proprietary.
    81	
    82	Finally, the project's scope is large, and we risk not finishing it within one semester.

-# Process: why the rules are shaped this way
-`CLAUDE.md` holds the rules, short enough to load every session. This file holds the
-reasoning behind them, the worked examples, and the one-time setup. Section numbers in
-parentheses name the `CLAUDE.md` rule each part explains.
-**Read this when** a rule looks arbitrary, when you are about to argue for an exception,
-or before the defense.
-## Why the git history is graded (§7)
-**This section is not advisory.** Our process grade is computed from transcripts
-corroborated against commits; the git history is itself a graded deliverable; and neither
-partner will break down a thousand-line diff to review it. A commit small enough to review
-in ninety seconds is a commit that actually gets reviewed.
-## Commit granularity (§7.3)
-**There is no line-count limit.** A commit is sized by *what it is responsible for*, not by
-how big the diff happens to be. A 200-line rewrite of a single function is **one** commit;
-splitting it would force the reviewer to hold half a function in their head across two
-reviews, which is worse than the problem it solves. Twenty lines spread across five
-unrelated concerns is **five** commits, even though it is small.
-**The test that decides it, every time:**
-> Can the reviewer evaluate this as a **single yes-or-no decision**?
-If approving requires accepting one part while objecting to another, it is more than one
-commit. If rejecting any part means rejecting the whole thing anyway, it is one commit —
-leave it alone.
-**The one-sentence test, restated.** State the commit's responsibility in one sentence
-without using "and". If you can, it is one commit no matter how many lines it took. If you
-cannot, split along the "and".
-### For code
-The unit is **one behavior, one function, or one design principle applied.**
-- Tests ship **in the same commit** as the behavior they test. Same responsibility.
-- A refactor is its own responsibility — never folded into a feature.
-- Formatting, renames, and file moves are **separate commits, labeled as such**, so the
-  reviewer skims them at speed instead of hunting for logic buried in noise.
-- Two subsystems means two commits, always, regardless of size.
-- **Every commit builds and passes tests on its own.** This is the one hard rule in this
-  section — it is what makes the history bisectable and each commit reviewable in isolation.
-**Size as a smell, not a limit.** Past roughly 400 changed lines, stop and re-apply the
-one-sentence test — large diffs *often* contain a smuggled second responsibility. If it
-survives the test, commit it as one unit and **say in the `WHY` why it is indivisible.**
-Then the reviewer knows the size was considered rather than accidental.
-### For documentation, Markdown, and data files
-The unit is **one resolved question or one decision** — not one file, not one section.
-- Closing one open question that touches a line in six tables across three files is **one
-  commit.** Splitting it is actively harmful: the reviewer can no longer see that the
-  change was applied *consistently*, which is the only thing worth checking.
-- A doc commit's diff is often wide and shallow. That is expected and correct.
-- Never mix a **content** change with a **reflow/reformat** of the same file — the content
-  change disappears into whitespace noise. Reformat separately, or not at all.
-- Never mix filling in a TODO with restructuring the section around it.
-- Never mix a decision's *record* with its *implementation* across files in a way that
-  hides one inside the other — but **do** keep a decision and the code that enacts it
-  together when they are genuinely one change.
-**The check:** `git show <commit>` should answer exactly one question a human asked. If it
-answers two, split. If it answers half of one, you committed too early.
-### For schematics (§7.12)
-Commit granularity for `electricalDrawing/` follows the documentation rule, not the code
-rule: the unit is **one functional block or one resolved electrical question**. Wiring the
-whole Power block is one commit even if it moves fifty symbols. Renumbering references
-across the sheet is a separate, labeled commit — never folded into a wiring change, for
-exactly the reason formatting is never folded into logic.
-## A commit message, worked (§7.4)
-The format itself is `.gitmessage` (enable it with
-`git config commit.template .gitmessage`). A real example:
-```text
-M3 ipc: refuse push on full ring instead of overwriting
-WHAT:   ring_push now returns false and increments an overrun counter when
-        head - tail == RING_CAPACITY, rather than wrapping over slot[tail].
-WHY:    DECISIONS.md B.3 — a silent overwrite is a gap in the record, and a
-        gap in the record is a gap in the diagnosis.
-REVIEW: The memory ordering on the tail load. I used acquire so the producer
-        cannot see a stale tail and wrongly declare the ring full; I am least
-        sure whether relaxed would be sufficient here.
-VERIFY: make && make test && make asan — all green, test_ring 3/3.
-## Pull requests (§7.5)
-- **A PR is sized by its claim, not its diff.** If the title needs "and", split it. If a
-  reviewer would have to approve part and object to part, split it. A PR that implements
-  one coherent thing is the right size even when that thing was large — but say so in the
-  body, and lay out the commit-by-commit list so the reviewer has a path through it.
-- **Past ~10 commits or ~600 changed lines, re-apply the test rather than obey a number.**
-  Most PRs that big contain two claims; the ones that genuinely do not are fine.
-- **Draft at the first commit**, not at the end — so the partner can watch it grow and
-  object early instead of at the finish line.
-- The "What I am least sure about" paragraph must not be empty. If everything is certain,
-  you have not thought hard enough about the diff.
-- If a PR needs a diagram, an annotated log excerpt, or a timing capture to be
-  understandable — put it in the PR body. Making the reviewer reconstruct context is how
-  reviews stop happening.
-## The merge gate (§7.6)
-**If the reviewer does not understand a line, the pull request does not merge.**
-The remedy is never "trust it." The remedy is, in order of preference:
-1. Claude explains it in a PR comment, in plain language, tied to the requirement.
-2. The commit is split further, so each piece is obvious on its own.
-3. The code is rewritten more simply, even at a cost in elegance or a few instructions.
-A reviewer must be able to answer these about **any line** in the diff before approving —
-they are the demo-day question set, asked early:
-- What wakes this? What is it waiting on?
-- What happens to this file descriptor / this allocation when the child dies?
-- What is the error path, and what does it log?
-- Why can't this drop, duplicate, or reorder a sample?
-- Which requirement or decision made it this way rather than the obvious alternative?
-Neither partner approves a PR they could not defend at the keyboard, alone, on demo day.
-**Approving code you do not understand is the only unrecoverable mistake in this
-workflow** — it is 20 individual points, and the defense will find it.
-## Volume and distribution (§7.9)
-≥ 40 meaningful commits across the semester, **both partners well represented**. A history
-where one partner authored under a quarter of the substantive commits is probed hard at the
-individual defense. A pair of "final submission" commits is an automatic process-grade of
-zero **for both partners**.
-Commit *as you go*, inside the session. A session that produces one commit at the end has
-already lost the granularity this section exists to protect.
-## Repository settings (§7.10, humans, once)
-On GitHub, set on `main`: require a pull request before merging · require 1 approval ·
-dismiss stale approvals on new commits · require conversation resolution · block force
-pushes · block deletions. Enable **squash-merge only if** the squash message is rewritten
-to be meaningful — otherwise prefer merge commits, since our granular history *is* the
-deliverable and squashing destroys it.
-**As configured** (board item `ghsetup`, verified 2026-09-12): the `Main` ruleset has all
-six, with **merge commits only**.
-## Why issues, and why the board is generated (§7.11)
-**GitHub Issues replace the blockers list.** Anything that needs a human — a question, a
-decision, a measurement only one of us can take, a part that must be ordered — is an
-**issue**, not a paragraph buried in a doc or a session summary nobody re-reads.
-`docs/DECISIONS.md` keeps only what has been **decided** (plus the review queue).
-Everything still open lives on the board, where it has an owner, a milestone, and a
-visible position in the queue.
-The board is not project-management theater. It is a timestamped record that the questions
-were asked before the work, that a human answered them, and that the answer shaped the
-code — which is precisely the process the transcripts are graded against, corroborated by
-an independent system we did not write. How the board works: `docs/BOARD/BOARD.md`.
-## Hardware pull requests (§7.12)
-KiCad files are S-expression **text**, so hardware goes through the same branches, commits
-and pull requests as the C — with two additions, both of which exist because a reviewer

1	# The board: how work is tracked
2	
3	Every task, question and decision in this project lives in **`docs/board.toml`**.
4	GitHub issues and the `carwatch` project board are *derived* from that file by
5	`tools/board_sync.py`. Nothing is typed directly into the GitHub web UI except
6	answers, discussion, and closing an issue.
7	
8	```
9	docs/board.toml   ──▶  tools/board_sync.py  ──▶  GitHub issues + project board
10	(source of truth)      (reconciler)              (derived)
11	docs/board.lock.json   slug → issue number, committed so the mapping survives
12	```
13	
14	## Running it
15	
16	No bash, no Makefile — this runs anywhere Python 3.11+ and `gh` exist, including
17	PowerShell:
18	
19	```powershell
20	python tools/board_sync.py --status     # what is Ready, what is stuck, who owns it
21	python tools/board_sync.py --check      # report drift; exits 1 if anything would change
22	python tools/board_sync.py              # reconcile
23	python tools/board_sync.py --only oilq  # reconcile one item
24	```
25	
26	One-time setup per machine: `gh auth login`, then `gh auth refresh -s project`.
27	
28	`--status` is the session-start and Monday-morning command. It prints the column counts,
29	the Ready list grouped by owner, **every critical-path item that is not Ready and the
30	specific open issues holding it**, and each open question or decision with its age in days.
31	It writes nothing and costs two API reads.
32	
33	## What the reconciler guarantees
34	
35	- **Idempotent.** Running it twice does nothing the second time. `--check` exits 1 when
36	  anything would change, which is what CI gates on.
37	- **Surgical.** Issues absent from `board.toml` are never edited, closed, or
38	  removed from the board. They are listed at the end as unmanaged.
39	- **Additive.** Adding a task or a question is one `[[item]]` block plus a re-run.
40	  Nothing unrelated is disturbed and nothing has to be closed to make room.
41	- **Non-destructive about closure.** GitHub wins on closure. If a human closes an
42	  issue in the web UI, sync moves the card to Done and reports that `board.toml`
43	  is behind — it never reopens.
44	- **Guarded.** Items labeled `question`, `decision` or `hardware` are never closed by the
45	  tool without the explicit `--close-questions` flag, per CLAUDE.md §7.11 — those close
46	  when a human answers.
47	- **Loud about orphans.** Deleting an `[[item]]` leaves a live issue behind. Sync retires
48	  the slug in the lock file and reports the issue as still open rather than forgetting it.
49	  To cut scope, mark the item `status = "done"` and say why in its body; don't delete it.
50	
51	## What is generated
52	
53	Three things derive from `board.toml` and must never be hand-edited:
54	
55	| Derived thing | Where | Marker |
56	|---|---|---|
57	| Issue bodies' blocked-by list and decision link | GitHub | `<!-- board-sync:deps -->` |
58	| The milestone table | `docs/milestones.md` | `<!-- board-sync:milestones -->` |
59	| slug → issue number | `docs/board.lock.json` | (whole file) |
60	
61	**Milestone dates are written in exactly one place**: the `[[milestone]]` blocks here.
62	Sync patches the GitHub due dates *and* regenerates the table in `docs/milestones.md`
63	between its markers, including a progress column counting closed issues per milestone.
64	When D-008 resolves, that is one edit in `board.toml` and one sync — the three cannot
65	disagree. Every word of exit criteria below that table is hand-written and is left alone.
66	
67	## Who owns what text
68	
69	`board.toml` owns the issue title and body. The tool rewrites them on GitHub, so
70	**edit the prose here, not in the web UI** — a body edited on GitHub is
71	overwritten on the next sync. The single exception is the region between the
72	`<!-- board-sync:deps -->` markers, which the tool computes from `blocked_by`:
73	it renders the `Blocked by: #12, #15` line and adds or removes the `blocked`
74	label as blockers open and close.
75	
76	## The loop
77	
78	1. A block sits in the **Backlog** column, labeled `question` or `decision`.
79	   Claude may never close those on its own.
80	2. Camden and Lance answer it — in the issue thread, or in a Claude Code session.
81	3. Claude factors the answer through the repo: `docs/DECISIONS.md` gets the
82	   decision, `docs/PLAN.md` and the affected docs get the consequence, and the
83	   one or two `[[item]]` entries the answer actually changed get updated —
84	   new tasks added, dead ones marked `status = "done"`, dependencies rewired.
85	4. `python tools/board_sync.py` pushes exactly that delta.
86	5. One commit contains the answer, its consequences, and the board move.
87	
88	## Editing `board.toml`
89	
90	```toml
91	[[item]]
92	slug = "oilpressure-sender"          # permanent identity. Never reuse, never renumber.
93	milestone = "M2"
94	labels = ["hardware", "critical-path"]
95	owner = "camden"                     # key into [people]; omit for unassigned
96	blocked_by = ["oilq"]                # slugs, never issue numbers
97	decision = "D-009"                   # optional; must exist in docs/DECISIONS.md
98	status = "ready"                     # optional; omit and sync infers backlog/ready
99	title = "M2 hardware: fit an analog oil-pressure sender"
100	body = '''
101	Prose. Markdown. Owned by this file.
102	'''
103	```
104	
105	`status` values: `backlog`, `blocked`, `ready`, `in-progress`, `in-review`, `done`.
106	Omit it and the tool picks the column: **Backlog** while any blocker is still
107	open, **Ready** the moment nothing blocks it, **Done** once the issue is closed.
108	So answering one question can move several cards into Ready on the next sync —
109	that is the board telling you what became workable.
110	
111	Set `status` by hand to override. `blocked` is reserved for waiting on something
112	that is *not* another item: a shipment, a reply from the professor, Lance.
113	
114	`decision` renders a link line into the managed region of the issue. Any `D-###` named
115	in a body or a `decision` field that is *not* in `docs/DECISIONS.md` is reported at the
116	end of every run, so a typo'd ID cannot sit in an issue pointing at nothing.
117	
118	## What stops a bad edit
119	
120	The tool refuses to run on a manifest with a duplicate slug, an unknown `owner`, an
121	undeclared milestone or label, a malformed `decision`, an empty body, a `blocked_by`
122	pointing at a slug that does not exist, or a dependency cycle — so a malformed edit fails
123	before it can touch GitHub.
124	
125	`tools/test_board.py` checks the rest offline and runs inside `make test`, because
126	`board.toml` is a graded artifact and deserves the same gate as the C: title convention,
127	slug format, exactly one kind label, no hand-set `blocked` label, no duplicate
128	`blocked_by`, milestone field completeness, and that **at least one open item is actually
129	startable** — a dependency edit that walls off the whole board is otherwise invisible.
130	
131	## CI
132	
133	`.github/workflows/board.yml`:
134	
135	- **manifest** — `python tools/test_board.py`, offline, on every push and PR.
136	- **drift** — `board_sync.py --check --no-board`, fails if GitHub no longer matches
137	  `board.toml`. This is the one that catches a forgotten sync. `--no-board` keeps it inside
138	  `GITHUB_TOKEN`'s reach; user-level Projects would need a PAT, and the board follows from
139	  the issues anyway.
140	- **pr-closes-issue** — every PR body must contain `Closes #<n>` per CLAUDE.md §7.11.
141	  Currently `continue-on-error: true` as a soft launch; **remove that line on 2026-09-26**
142	  once the habit is set.
143	
144	## Where this came from
145	
146	`tools/bootstrap_board.sh` was a one-shot generator: it created everything or nothing,
147	refused to run a second time, never touched the project board, and swallowed its own
148	errors. It was deleted; git history has it, and the plan text it carried is now the
149	`[[item]]` blocks in `board.toml`. The full diagnosis is PROMPTLOG episode E-01.

# Problem memo — carwatch (Camden Thomas, Lance Baron)

## The user

An average car owner who drives to work every day uses a car very differently from someone
who works from home and takes one road trip a year, yet both are handed the same
recommended maintenance schedule. That contrast is the thesis of this project: the same
oil-change sticker says 5,000 miles to both cars, and the cars disagree.

## The problem

Maintenance intervals are generalizations, and the sticker on the windshield knows nothing
about how this engine has actually been run: a commuter that never reaches operating
temperature and a highway car with the same odometer reading have not aged the same way.
Because of that, the error runs in both directions, and both are expensive, whether it is
oil changed far earlier than it needed to be or an engine run on oil that lost its
pressure margin weeks ago. The frustrating part is that the car's own sensors already
measure everything needed to tell these cases apart. What is missing is a device that
records that data continuously, learns what normal looks like for this car, and flags a
developing fault before the check-engine light of doom puts its owner on an hour-long bus
ride.

## Why a device

The signal we are after is a slow trend across weeks of driving, and it is only
interpretable with the cold starts, the short trips, and the long pulls, *all* of them,
not just the drives someone remembered to open an app for. A phone app is present only for
the trips its owner thought to instrument, which is a biased sample of exactly the variable
being measured. Moreover, the interesting moment is never the moment anyone is looking: it
is the third cold start of a February week, when warm-up took ninety seconds longer than it
did in January, and nobody is holding a phone then. The device, by contrast, is already in
the car, awake at key-on and recording before anyone has decided anything is wrong.
Finally, the data stays in the car, with no account, no upload, and no fleet telematics
company holding a log of everywhere this person drove.

## The sensors

The device reads the vehicle's own sensors through the OBD2 port: oil pressure, coolant
temperature, intake air temperature, MAP, O2 / fuel trims, RPM, and engine load. These
sensors cooperate rather than merely coexist, because **no one of them means anything
alone.** Oil pressure, for example, is a function of RPM and oil temperature, so the
diagnostic signal is the *residual* left after normalizing for both, and reaching that one
conclusion takes all three sensors. In the same way, fuel trim is only interpretable
against load, and coolant temperature only indicts a thermostat once ambient temperature
and load have been accounted for. As a result, every verdict this device produces requires
at least two sensors to agree on something a single threshold cannot see.

## The mechanisms

Our first choice is **mechanism D, custom append-only storage with crash consistency**,
because the power is cut mid-write every time the key turns off, so the storage layer
never gets a clean shutdown and must recover a torn tail on every boot. We pair it with
**mechanism E, a multi-process architecture with a supervisor**, because a recorder that
dies silently has harmed its owner, who believes it is still on duty; running capture,
storage, and analysis as separate processes means a crash in the analysis cannot take the
recording down with it.

## The risk

The primary risk, named honestly, is time: the oil-life trend needs a real oil interval to
develop, and that is calendar time we cannot buy back by working harder in Week 14, so
baseline collection starts at M2 or it does not happen. The second risk is the OBD2
protocol itself, which each manufacturer implements differently across four different
*data frames*; even once those are handled, a received signal may be impossible to decode
because the manufacturer keeps its meaning proprietary. Finally, the project's scope is
large, and we risk not finishing it within one semester.

## The user

who works from home and takes one road trip a year, yet both are handed the same
recommended maintenance schedule.

That contrast is the thesis: the same oil-change sticker says 5,000 miles to both cars,
and the cars disagree.

## The problem

> Observable and costly: what goes wrong, how often, what it costs in money or worry.

Maintenance intervals are generalizations. The sticker on the windshield knows nothing
about how this engine has actually been run — a commuter that never reaches operating
temperature and a highway car with the same odometer reading have not aged the same way.
The error runs in both directions, and both are expensive: oil changed far earlier than it
needed to be, or an engine run on oil that lost its pressure margin weeks ago.

The car's own sensors already measure everything needed to tell these cases apart. What is
missing is a device that records that data continuously, learns what normal looks like for
this car, and flags a developing fault before the check-engine light of doom puts its
owner on an hour-long bus ride.

## Why a device

> The 3 a.m. test: why must something be physically present and always awake? And why

have the cold starts, the short trips, and the long pulls — *all* of them, not the
drives someone remembered to open an app for. A phone app is present for the trips you
thought to instrument, which is a biased sample of exactly the variable being measured.

The interesting moment is also never the moment anyone is looking: it is the third cold
start of a February week when warm-up took ninety seconds longer than it did in
January. Nobody is holding a phone then. The device is in the car, awake at key-on,
recording before anyone has decided anything is wrong.

And the data stays in the car. No account, no upload, no fleet telematics company
holding a log of everywhere this person drove.

## The sensors

> Which two (or more) and how they **cooperate** rather than coexist.

The vehicle's own sensors, read via the OBD2 port: oil pressure, coolant temperature,

They cooperate because **no one of them means anything alone.** Oil pressure is a
function of RPM and oil temperature; the diagnostic signal is the *residual* after

trim is only interpretable against load. Coolant temperature only indicts a thermostat

> First guess at two menu items, one sentence of justification each. May change by M2.

every single time the key turns off, so the storage layer never gets a clean shutdown
and must recover a torn tail on every boot.

**E — multi-process architecture with a supervisor.** A recorder that dies silently has
harmed its owner, who believes it is on duty; capture, storage, and analysis run as

The primary risk, named honestly: the oil-life trend needs a real oil interval to develop,

# Plan: docs/milestones.md becomes the board

## Context

Camden wants one list to drive everything. He edited `docs/milestones.md` directly: he
trimmed M0, checked off M1, and moved "Hardware ordered" into M1. That edit is stashed
on `camden/m1/problem-polish`, with a patch copy in the scratchpad. The checklist format
is easy for a human to maintain.

**What is wrong today:**

- `docs/BOARD/board.toml` holds 99 items with rich bodies, dependencies and labels.
- It generates about 100 GitHub issues that are too much to follow.
- It duplicates the milestone exit criteria.

**Goal:** tick a box in `docs/milestones.md`, run `python tools/board_sync.py`, and
GitHub follows. Nothing is lost:

- every existing issue becomes a checkbox under its milestone;
- the open decisions become `Decide:` lines;
- `board.toml` is retired, and issue bodies stay on GitHub where they already are.

## The format (what Camden edits)

```markdown
| M | Deliverable | Week | Due | Team hrs | Progress |        <- dates hand-edited here;
| --- | ...                                        |          Progress filled by sync

## M2 — Design document; sensors alive; baseline starts

- [ ] **Both sensors alive: real Mode 01 replies from a real car** <!-- #20 -->
- [ ] M2 hardware: Bluetooth OBD2 adapter bring-up on the Pi, no car `bench` @camden <!-- #18 -->
- [ ] Decide: fsync discipline, batch size and interval `fsync` @lance <!-- #23 -->
- [x] M2 hardware: two-node bench CAN bus (cut, D-015) `twonode` <!-- #19 -->
```

**How the parts of a line work:**

- **Checkbox:** unchecked means the issue is open, and `[x]` closes it on the next sync.
- **Text:** becomes the issue title.
- **`@camden` / `@lance`:** sets the assignee.
- **`` `slug` ``:** kept as the human name that PLAN.md and DECISIONS.md already cite.
- **`<!-- #n -->`:** the hidden link to the issue. Sync writes it the first time; it does
  not render. Reword, reorder, or move a line to another milestone, and it stays the same
  issue.
- **Bold lines:** the broad exit criteria, which are issues too. Each milestone lists its
  exit criteria first, then its tasks, so the balance is visible.

## Sync rules (new `tools/board_sync.py`)

| In the file | On GitHub |
| --- | --- |
| line with no tag | create issue, milestone from the section, assignee from `@`; tag written back into the line |
| `[x]`, issue open | close it |
| `[ ]`, issue closed by a human on GitHub | tick the box in the file and report it (never reopen, same as today) |
| text differs from title | retitle |
| line moved to another milestone | re-milestone |
| tag no longer in the file | report as orphan; never close |
| table `Due` column | GitHub milestone due dates; `Progress` column regenerated as checked/total |
| project board (if the token has `project` scope) | open → Ready, closed → Done; otherwise skipped with the one-line fix |

1	# Problem memo — carwatch (Camden Thomas, Lance Baron)
2	
3	
4	## The user
5	
6	An average car owner who drives everyday to work, is vastly different from someone who
7	works from home and does the yearly road trip, although the recommended maintenance is
8	still the same. 
9	
10	The point of two users is the thesis: the same oil-change sticker says 5,000 miles to
11	both cars, and the cars disagree.
12	
13	## The problem
14	
15	> Observable and costly: what goes wrong, how often, what it costs in money or worry.
16	
17	Maintenance intervals are generalizations. The sticker on the windshield knows nothing
18	about how this engine has actually been run — a commuter that never reaches operating
19	temperature and a highway car with the same odometer reading have not aged the same
20	way. The consequence runs both directions and both are expensive: oil changed far
21	earlier than it needed to be, or an engine run on oil that lost its pressure margin
22	weeks ago. While the sensors already present do a great job tracking all the need information,
23	people just need a device to monitor and store this data to learn the car and predict failures before the check engine light of doom puts you on the hour long bus ride.
24	
25	## Why a device
26	
27	> The 3 a.m. test: why must something be physically present and always awake? And why
28	> doesn't a phone app already solve this?
29	
30	The signal is a slow trend across weeks of driving, and it is only interpretable if you
31	have the cold starts, the short trips, and the long pulls — *all* of them, not the
32	drives someone remembered to open an app for. A phone app is present for the trips you
33	thought to instrument, which is a biased sample of exactly the variable being measured.
34	
35	The interesting moment is also never the moment anyone is looking: it is the third cold
36	start of a February week where warm-up took ninety seconds longer than it did in
37	January. Nobody is holding a phone then. The device is in the car, awake at key-on,
38	recording before anyone has decided anything is wrong.
39	
40	And the data stays in the car. No account, no upload, no fleet telematics company
41	holding a log of everywhere this person drove.
42	
43	## The sensors
44	
45	> Which two (or more) and how they **cooperate** rather than coexist.
46	
47	The vehicle's own sensors, read via the OBD2 port: oil pressure, coolant temperature,
48	intake air temperature, MAP, O2 / fuel trims, RPM, engine load.
49	
50	They cooperate because **no one of them means anything alone.** Oil pressure is a
51	function of RPM and oil temperature; the diagnostic signal is the *residual* after
52	normalizing for both, which requires all three sensors to reach one conclusion. Fuel
53	trim is only interpretable against load. Coolant temperature only indicts a thermostat
54	once ambient temperature and load have been accounted for. Every verdict this device
55	produces requires at least two sensors to agree on something a single threshold cannot
56	see.
57	
58	
59	## The mechanisms
60	
61	> First guess at two menu items, one sentence of justification each. May change by M2.
62	
63	**D — custom append-only storage with crash consistency.** The power is cut mid-write
64	every single time the key turns off, so the storage layer never gets a clean shutdown
65	and must recover a torn tail on every boot.
66	
67	**E — multi-process architecture with a supervisor.** A recorder that dies silently has
68	harmed its owner, who believes it is on duty; capture, storage and analysis run as
69	separate processes so that a crash in the analysis cannot take the recording down with it.
70	
71	## The risk
72	
73	The primary risk, named honestly: the oil-life trend needs a real oil interval to develop,
74	and that is calendar time we cannot buy back by working harder in Week 14. Baseline
75	collection starts at M2 or it does not happen.
76	
77	Secondly there lies another risk of how the OBD protocol works, were each car implements it differently, there being 4 different *data frames*, and even if we get past those worries, decoding the recieved signal may not be possible due it being proprietary to the manufacturer. The scale of the project is quite large, and we risk not completeing the project within one semester.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
board_sync.py — make GitHub match the checklist in docs/milestones.md (D-020).

docs/milestones.md is the board. Every checkbox line under a `## M<n>` heading is
one GitHub issue:

    - [ ] M2 hardware: first live capture from a real car `firstcap` @camden <!-- #20 -->

  [ ] / [x]        open / closed. Tick the box and sync: the issue closes.
  text             the issue title ("M<n>: " is prefixed if the text has none)
  `slug`           optional trailing name other docs cite; not part of the title
  @camden @lance   optional assignee
  <!-- #20 -->     the issue number. Written by sync the first time; never type it.

What sync does, and never does:
  * a line with no tag becomes a new issue, and the tag is written back
  * [x] on an open issue closes it
  * an issue a human closed on GitHub ticks its box here; sync never reopens
  * retitles, re-milestones and assigns to match the line
  * the table's Due column sets GitHub milestone due dates; Progress is recounted
  * issue bodies and labels are left alone: GitHub owns them
  * an open issue that no line mentions is reported, never closed

Usage (Python 3.11+, `gh` authenticated):

    python tools/board_sync.py              reconcile, then write tags/ticks back
    python tools/board_sync.py --check      report drift; exit 1 if anything would change
    python tools/board_sync.py --status     open boxes per milestone, by owner
    python tools/board_sync.py --no-board   skip the project board (CI: no PAT)
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
LIST_DOC = REPO_ROOT / "docs" / "milestones.md"

PEOPLE = {"camden": "CamdenThomas", "lance": "Lance-Baron"}
PROJECT_NUMBER = 1          # the `carwatch` project linked to the repo
WRAP = 90                   # .markdownlint.jsonc line length (D-018)

TABLE_OPEN = "<!-- board-sync:milestones -->"
TABLE_CLOSE = "<!-- /board-sync:milestones -->"

SECTION_RE = re.compile(r"^## (M[0-6])\b")
ITEM_RE = re.compile(r"^- \[([ xX])\] (.*)$")
TAG_RE = re.compile(r"\s*<!--\s*#(\d+)\s*-->")
OWNER_RE = re.compile(r"(?<!\S)@(\w+)")
SLUG_RE = re.compile(r"\s+`([a-z][a-z0-9-]{1,30})`$")
ROW_RE = re.compile(r"^\|\s*(M[0-6])\s*\|")


class Fail(Exception):
    pass


def say(msg: str = "") -> None:
    enc = getattr(sys.stdout, "encoding", None) or "utf-8"
    print(msg.encode(enc, "replace").decode(enc), flush=True)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ parsing

@dataclass
class Item:
    milestone: str
    checked: bool
    text: str                  # the item's words, tag/owner/slug removed
    slug: str | None
    owner: str | None          # key into PEOPLE
    number: int | None         # the tag
    first: int                 # line index of "- [ ]"
    last: int                  # line index of the item's final continuation line

    @property
    def title(self) -> str:
        t = self.text.replace("**", "").strip()
        return t if re.match(r"M[0-6]\b", t) else f"{self.milestone}: {t}"


@dataclass
class Board:
    lines: list[str]
    items: list[Item] = field(default_factory=list)
    rows: dict[str, list[str]] = field(default_factory=dict)   # M -> table cells


def parse(text: str) -> Board:
    """Split docs/milestones.md into table rows and checkbox items."""
    b = Board(lines=text.split("\n"))
    section = None
    in_table = False
    i = 0
    while i < len(b.lines):
        line = b.lines[i]
        if line.strip() == TABLE_OPEN:
            in_table = True
        elif line.strip() == TABLE_CLOSE:
            in_table = False
        elif in_table and ROW_RE.match(line):
            cells = [c.strip() for c in line.strip().strip("|").split("|")]
            if len(cells) != 6:
                raise Fail(f"milestones.md:{i+1}: table row needs 6 cells: {line}")
            b.rows[cells[0]] = cells
        if line.startswith("## "):
            m = SECTION_RE.match(line)
            section = m.group(1) if m else None
        m = ITEM_RE.match(line)
        if m:
            if section is None:
                raise Fail(f"milestones.md:{i+1}: checkbox outside an `## M<n>` section")
            j = i
            while j + 1 < len(b.lines) and b.lines[j + 1].startswith("  ") \
                    and b.lines[j + 1].strip():
                j += 1
            raw = " ".join([m.group(2)] + [x.strip() for x in b.lines[i + 1:j + 1]])
            tags = TAG_RE.findall(raw)
            if len(tags) > 1:
                raise Fail(f"milestones.md:{i+1}: more than one issue tag on one item")
            raw = TAG_RE.sub("", raw).strip()
            owners = OWNER_RE.findall(raw)
            for o in owners:
                if o not in PEOPLE:
                    raise Fail(f"milestones.md:{i+1}: unknown owner @{o} "
                               f"(known: {', '.join('@' + p for p in PEOPLE)})")
            raw = OWNER_RE.sub("", raw).strip()
            sm = SLUG_RE.search(raw)
            slug = sm.group(1) if sm else None
            if sm:
                raw = raw[:sm.start()].rstrip()
            b.items.append(Item(section, m.group(1) != " ", re.sub(r"\s+", " ", raw),
                                slug, owners[0] if owners else None,
                                int(tags[0]) if tags else None, i, j))
            i = j
        i += 1
    seen: dict[int, int] = {}
    for it in b.items:
        if it.number is not None:
            if it.number in seen:
                raise Fail(f"milestones.md:{it.first+1}: issue #{it.number} is also on "
                           f"line {seen[it.number]+1}")
            seen[it.number] = it.first
    return b


def render(b: Board) -> str:
    """Rewrite the table's Progress column from the checkboxes."""
    out = []
    for line in b.lines:
        m = ROW_RE.match(line)
        if m and m.group(1) in b.rows:
            ms = m.group(1)
            mine = [it for it in b.items if it.milestone == ms]
            done = sum(it.checked for it in mine)
            icon = "—" if not mine else "✅" if done == len(mine) else "🟡" if done else "⬜"
            cells = b.rows[ms][:5] + [f"{icon} {done}/{len(mine)}" if mine else "—"]
            line = "| " + " | ".join(cells) + " |"
        out.append(line)
    return "\n".join(out)


def set_tag(b: Board, it: Item, number: int) -> None:
    """Append `<!-- #n -->` to the item's last line, wrapping to stay within WRAP."""
    tag = f"<!-- #{number} -->"
    last = b.lines[it.last]
    if len(last) + 1 + len(tag) <= WRAP:
        b.lines[it.last] = f"{last} {tag}"
    else:
        b.lines.insert(it.last + 1, "      " + tag)
        for other in b.items:
            if other.first > it.last:
                other.first += 1
                other.last += 1
        it.last += 1
    it.number = number


def set_checked(b: Board, it: Item) -> None:
    b.lines[it.first] = b.lines[it.first].replace("- [ ]", "- [x]", 1)
    it.checked = True


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------- gh

class Gh:
    def __init__(self, dry: bool):
        self.dry, self.reads, self.writes, self.pending = dry, 0, 0, 0

    def run(self, args: list[str]) -> tuple[int, str, str]:
        p = subprocess.run(["gh", *args], capture_output=True, text=True,
                           encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
        return p.returncode, p.stdout.strip(), p.stderr.strip()

    def read_json(self, args: list[str], default=None):
        self.reads += 1
        code, out, err = self.run(args)
        if code != 0:
            if default is not None:
                return default
            raise Fail(f"gh {' '.join(args)}\n  -> {err}")
        return json.loads(out) if out else default

    def write(self, args: list[str], label: str) -> str:
        if self.dry:
            self.pending += 1
            say(f"    would: {label}")
            return ""
        self.writes += 1
        code, out, err = self.run(args)
        if code != 0:
            raise Fail(f"{label}\n  gh {' '.join(args)}\n  -> {err}")
        say(f"  {label}")
        return out


# -------------------------------------------------------------------- sync

def sync_milestones(gh: Gh, repo: str, b: Board) -> None:
    have = {m["title"]: m for m in
            gh.read_json(["api", f"repos/{repo}/milestones?state=all&per_page=100"], [])}
    for ms, cells in b.rows.items():
        due, desc = cells[3], cells[1]
        if not re.fullmatch(r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}", due):
            raise Fail(f"milestones.md: {ms} Due must be YYYY-MM-DD, got {due!r}")
        cur = have.get(ms)
        if cur is None:
            gh.write(["api", f"repos/{repo}/milestones", "-f", f"title={ms}",
                      "-f", f"due_on={due}T23:59:59Z", "-f", f"description={desc}"],
                     f"create milestone {ms}")
        elif (cur.get("due_on") or "")[:10] != due or (cur.get("description") or "") != desc:
            gh.write(["api", "-X", "PATCH", f"repos/{repo}/milestones/{cur['number']}",
                      "-f", f"due_on={due}T23:59:59Z", "-f", f"description={desc}"],
                     f"update milestone {ms} (due {due})")


def sync_issues(gh: Gh, b: Board) -> tuple[bool, list[str]]:
    """Returns (file changed, report lines)."""
    issues = {r["number"]: r for r in gh.read_json(
        ["issue", "list", "--state", "all", "--limit", "1000",
         "--json", "number,title,state,milestone,assignees"], [])}
    changed, report = False, []
    for it in list(b.items):
        if it.number is None:
            label = "decision" if re.match(r"(Decide:|M[0-6] (decision|question))",
                                           it.text) else "task"
            cmd = ["issue", "create", "--title", it.title, "--milestone", it.milestone,
                   "--label", label, "--body",
                   f"Tracked in `docs/milestones.md`, {it.milestone}. Tick the box there "
                   "and run `python tools/board_sync.py`."]
            if it.owner:
                cmd += ["--assignee", PEOPLE[it.owner]]
            url = gh.write(cmd, f"create '{it.title}'")
            if gh.dry:
                continue
            set_tag(b, it, int(url.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]))
            changed = True
            issues[it.number] = {"number": it.number, "title": it.title, "state": "OPEN",
                                 "milestone": {"title": it.milestone},
                                 "assignees": [{"login": PEOPLE[it.owner]}]
                                 if it.owner else []}
        issue = issues.get(it.number)
        if issue is None:
            raise Fail(f"milestones.md:{it.first+1}: #{it.number} does not exist on GitHub")
        edit = []
        if issue["title"] != it.title:
            edit += ["--title", it.title]
        if (issue.get("milestone") or {}).get("title") != it.milestone:
            edit += ["--milestone", it.milestone]
        if it.owner and PEOPLE[it.owner] not in {a["login"] for a in issue["assignees"]}:
            edit += ["--add-assignee", PEOPLE[it.owner]]
        if edit:
            gh.write(["issue", "edit", str(it.number), *edit],
                     f"edit #{it.number}: {' '.join(e for e in edit if e.startswith('--'))}")
        closed = issue["state"].upper() == "CLOSED"
        if it.checked and not closed:
            gh.write(["issue", "close", str(it.number), "--reason", "completed"],
                     f"close #{it.number} (ticked)")
        elif closed and not it.checked:
            set_checked(b, it)
            changed = True
            report.append(f"#{it.number} was closed on GitHub; ticked its box")
    listed = {it.number for it in b.items}
    for n, r in sorted(issues.items()):
        if n not in listed and r["state"].upper() == "OPEN":
            report.append(f"#{n} is open on GitHub but on no line: {r['title']}")
    return changed, report


def sync_board(gh: Gh, repo: str, b: Board) -> str | None:
    projects = gh.read_json(["project", "list", "--owner", "@me", "--format", "json"], {})
    proj = next((p for p in projects.get("projects", [])
                 if p["number"] == PROJECT_NUMBER), None)
    if proj is None:
        return "board skipped: cannot read projects (run `gh auth refresh -s project`)"
    pnum, pid = str(PROJECT_NUMBER), proj["id"]
    fields = gh.read_json(["project", "field-list", pnum, "--owner", "@me",
                           "--format", "json"], {"fields": []})
    status = next((f for f in fields["fields"] if f["name"].lower() == "status"), None)
    opts = {o["name"].lower(): o["id"] for o in (status or {}).get("options", [])}
    cards = {(c.get("content") or {}).get("number"): c for c in gh.read_json(
        ["project", "item-list", pnum, "--owner", "@me", "--format", "json",
         "--limit", "1000"], {"items": []})["items"]}
    for it in b.items:
        if it.number is None:
            continue
        card = cards.get(it.number)
        if card is None:
            out = gh.write(["project", "item-add", pnum, "--owner", "@me", "--url",
                            f"https://github.com/{repo}/issues/{it.number}",
                            "--format", "json"], f"add #{it.number} to the board")
            if gh.dry:
                continue
            card = json.loads(out)
        want = "done" if it.checked else "ready"
        oid = opts.get(want) or opts.get("todo")
        if status and oid and (card.get("status") or "").lower() != want:
            gh.write(["project", "item-edit", "--id", card["id"], "--project-id", pid,
                      "--field-id", status["id"], "--single-select-option-id", oid],
                     f"#{it.number} -> {want}")
    return None


def status(b: Board) -> None:
    for ms in b.rows:
        mine = [it for it in b.items if it.milestone == ms]
        open_ = [it for it in mine if not it.checked]
        say(f"{ms}  {len(mine) - len(open_)}/{len(mine)} done  (due {b.rows[ms][3]})")
        for owner in sorted({it.owner or "" for it in open_}):
            say(f"  {'@' + owner if owner else 'unassigned'}:")
            for it in open_:
                if (it.owner or "") == owner:
                    say(f"    #{it.number or '(new)'}  {it.text.replace('**', '')}")


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Make GitHub match docs/milestones.md.")
    ap.add_argument("--check", action="store_true", help="change nothing; exit 1 on drift")
    ap.add_argument("--status", action="store_true", help="print open boxes and stop")
    ap.add_argument("--no-board", action="store_true", help="skip the project board")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    original = LIST_DOC.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    b = parse(original)
    if args.status:
        status(b)
        return 0

    gh = Gh(dry=args.check)
    code, repo, err = gh.run(["repo", "view", "--json", "nameWithOwner",
                              "-q", ".nameWithOwner"])
    if code != 0:
        raise Fail(f"gh repo view -> {err}")
    say(f"repo: {repo}" + ("   [CHECK ONLY]" if args.check else ""))
    sync_milestones(gh, repo, b)
    changed, report = sync_issues(gh, b)
    note = None if args.no_board else sync_board(gh, repo, b)

    new = render(b)
    if new != original:
        if args.check:
            gh.pending += 1
            say("    would: rewrite docs/milestones.md (tags, ticks or progress)")
        else:
            LIST_DOC.write_text(new, encoding="utf-8")
            say("  wrote docs/milestones.md")
    for r in report:
        say(f"  ! {r}")
    if note:
        say(f"  {note}")
    say(f"reads {gh.reads}, writes {gh.writes}")
    if args.check and gh.pending:
        say(f"(check only — {gh.pending} change(s) pending)")
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        sys.exit(main())
    except Fail as e:
        say(f"\nERROR: {e}")
        sys.exit(1)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        say("\ninterrupted — re-run to continue")
        sys.exit(130)

    tag = f"<!-- #{number} -->"
    last = b.lines[it.last]
    if len(last) + 1 + len(tag) <= WRAP:
        b.lines[it.last] = f"{last} {tag}"
    else:
        b.lines.insert(it.last + 1, "      " + tag)
        for other in b.items:
            if other.first > it.last:
                other.first += 1
                other.last += 1
        it.last += 1
    it.number = number


def set_checked(b: Board, it: Item) -> None:
    b.lines[it.first] = b.lines[it.first].replace("- [ ]", "- [x]", 1)
    it.checked = True


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------- gh

class Gh:
    def __init__(self, dry: bool):
        self.dry, self.reads, self.writes, self.pending = dry, 0, 0, 0

    def run(self, args: list[str]) -> tuple[int, str, str]:
        p = subprocess.run(["gh", *args], capture_output=True, text=True,
                           encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
        return p.returncode, p.stdout.strip(), p.stderr.strip()

    def read_json(self, args: list[str], default=None):
        self.reads += 1
        code, out, err = self.run(args)
        if code != 0:
            if default is not None:
                return default
            raise Fail(f"gh {' '.join(args)}\n  -> {err}")
        return json.loads(out) if out else default

    def write(self, args: list[str], label: str) -> str:
        if self.dry:
            self.pending += 1
            say(f"    would: {label}")
            return ""
        self.writes += 1
        code, out, err = self.run(args)
        if code != 0:
            raise Fail(f"{label}\n  gh {' '.join(args)}\n  -> {err}")
        say(f"  {label}")
        return out


# -------------------------------------------------------------------- sync

def sync_milestones(gh: Gh, repo: str, b: Board) -> None:
    have = {m["title"]: m for m in
            gh.read_json(["api", f"repos/{repo}/milestones?state=all&per_page=100"], [])}
    for ms, cells in b.rows.items():
        due, desc = cells[3], cells[1]
        if not re.fullmatch(r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}", due):
            raise Fail(f"milestones.md: {ms} Due must be YYYY-MM-DD, got {due!r}")
        cur = have.get(ms)
        if cur is None:
            gh.write(["api", f"repos/{repo}/milestones", "-f", f"title={ms}",
                      "-f", f"due_on={due}T23:59:59Z", "-f", f"description={desc}"],
                     f"create milestone {ms}")
        elif (cur.get("due_on") or "")[:10] != due or (cur.get("description") or "") != desc:
            gh.write(["api", "-X", "PATCH", f"repos/{repo}/milestones/{cur['number']}",
                      "-f", f"due_on={due}T23:59:59Z", "-f", f"description={desc}"],
                     f"update milestone {ms} (due {due})")


def sync_issues(gh: Gh, b: Board) -> tuple[bool, list[str]]:
    """Returns (file changed, report lines)."""
    issues = {r["number"]: r for r in gh.read_json(
        ["issue", "list", "--state", "all", "--limit", "1000",
         "--json", "number,title,state,milestone,assignees"], [])}
    changed, report = False, []
    for it in list(b.items):
        if it.number is None:
            label = "decision" if re.match(r"(Decide:|M[0-6] (decision|question))",
                                           it.text) else "task"
            cmd = ["issue", "create", "--title", it.title, "--milestone", it.milestone,
                   "--label", label, "--body",
                   f"Tracked in `docs/milestones.md`, {it.milestone}. Tick the box there "
                   "and run `python tools/board_sync.py`."]
            if it.owner:
                cmd += ["--assignee", PEOPLE[it.owner]]
            url = gh.write(cmd, f"create '{it.title}'")
            if gh.dry:
                continue
            set_tag(b, it, int(url.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]))
            changed = True
            issues[it.number] = {"number": it.number, "title": it.title, "state": "OPEN",
                                 "milestone": {"title": it.milestone},
                                 "assignees": [{"login": PEOPLE[it.owner]}]
                                 if it.owner else []}
        issue = issues.get(it.number)
        if issue is None:
            raise Fail(f"milestones.md:{it.first+1}: #{it.number} does not exist on GitHub")
        edit = []
        if issue["title"] != it.title:
            edit += ["--title", it.title]
        if (issue.get("milestone") or {}).get("title") != it.milestone:
            edit += ["--milestone", it.milestone]
        if it.owner and PEOPLE[it.owner] not in {a["login"] for a in issue["assignees"]}:
            edit += ["--add-assignee", PEOPLE[it.owner]]
        if edit:
            gh.write(["issue", "edit", str(it.number), *edit],
                     f"edit #{it.number}: {' '.join(e for e in edit if e.startswith('--'))}")
        closed = issue["state"].upper() == "CLOSED"
        if it.checked and not closed:
            gh.write(["issue", "close", str(it.number), "--reason", "completed"],
                     f"close #{it.number} (ticked)")
        elif closed and not it.checked:
            set_checked(b, it)
            changed = True
            report.append(f"#{it.number} was closed on GitHub; ticked its box")
    listed = {it.number for it in b.items}
    for n, r in sorted(issues.items()):
        if n not in listed and r["state"].upper() == "OPEN":
            report.append(f"#{n} is open on GitHub but on no line: {r['title']}")
    return changed, report


def sync_board(gh: Gh, repo: str, b: Board) -> str | None:
    projects = gh.read_json(["project", "list", "--owner", "@me", "--format", "json"], {})
    proj = next((p for p in projects.get("projects", [])
                 if p["number"] == PROJECT_NUMBER), None)
    if proj is None:
        return "board skipped: cannot read projects (run `gh auth refresh -s project`)"
    pnum, pid = str(PROJECT_NUMBER), proj["id"]
    fields = gh.read_json(["project", "field-list", pnum, "--owner", "@me",
                           "--format", "json"], {"fields": []})
    status = next((f for f in fields["fields"] if f["name"].lower() == "status"), None)
    opts = {o["name"].lower(): o["id"] for o in (status or {}).get("options", [])}
    cards = {(c.get("content") or {}).get("number"): c for c in gh.read_json(
        ["project", "item-list", pnum, "--owner", "@me", "--format", "json",
         "--limit", "1000"], {"items": []})["items"]}
    for it in b.items:
        if it.number is None:
            continue
        card = cards.get(it.number)
        if card is None:
            out = gh.write(["project", "item-add", pnum, "--owner", "@me", "--url",
                            f"https://github.com/{repo}/issues/{it.number}",
                            "--format", "json"], f"add #{it.number} to the board")
            if gh.dry:
                continue
            card = json.loads(out)
        want = "done" if it.checked else "ready"
        oid = opts.get(want) or opts.get("todo")
        if status and oid and (card.get("status") or "").lower() != want:
            gh.write(["project", "item-edit", "--id", card["id"], "--project-id", pid,
                      "--field-id", status["id"], "--single-select-option-id", oid],
                     f"#{it.number} -> {want}")
    return None


def status(b: Board) -> None:
    for ms in b.rows:
        mine = [it for it in b.items if it.milestone == ms]
        open_ = [it for it in mine if not it.checked]
        say(f"{ms}  {len(mine) - len(open_)}/{len(mine)} done  (due {b.rows[ms][3]})")
        for owner in sorted({it.owner or "" for it in open_}):
            say(f"  {'@' + owner if owner else 'unassigned'}:")
            for it in open_:
                if (it.owner or "") == owner:
                    say(f"    #{it.number or '(new)'}  {it.text.replace('**', '')}")


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Make GitHub match docs/milestones.md.")
    ap.add_argument("--check", action="store_true", help="change nothing; exit 1 on drift")
    ap.add_argument("--status", action="store_true", help="print open boxes and stop")
    ap.add_argument("--no-board", action="store_true", help="skip the project board")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    original = LIST_DOC.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    b = parse(original)
    if args.status:
        status(b)
        return 0

    gh = Gh(dry=args.check)
    code, repo, err = gh.run(["repo", "view", "--json", "nameWithOwner",
                              "-q", ".nameWithOwner"])
    if code != 0:
        raise Fail(f"gh repo view -> {err}")
    say(f"repo: {repo}" + ("   [CHECK ONLY]" if args.check else ""))
    sync_milestones(gh, repo, b)
    changed, report = sync_issues(gh, b)
    note = None if args.no_board else sync_board(gh, repo, b)

    new = render(b)
    if new != original:
        if args.check:
            gh.pending += 1
            say("    would: rewrite docs/milestones.md (tags, ticks or progress)")
        else:
            LIST_DOC.write_text(new, encoding="utf-8")
            say("  wrote docs/milestones.md")
    for r in report:
        say(f"  ! {r}")
    if note:
        say(f"  {note}")
    say(f"reads {gh.reads}, writes {gh.writes}")
    if args.check and gh.pending:
        say(f"(check only — {gh.pending} change(s) pending)")
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        sys.exit(main())
    except Fail as e:
        say(f"\nERROR: {e}")
        sys.exit(1)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        say("\ninterrupted — re-run to continue")
        sys.exit(130)
